9.23.0.description:
> 🤖 *This PR was created by the create-pr skill.*

## Summary

- emit a dedicated ES5 aggregate bundle from production UMD builds
- publish the new bundle through existing npm package and CDN snapshot collection
- update Babylon Native CI to consume prebuilt ES5 artifacts instead of downleveling after download

## Details

The UMD build helper now supports an explicit aggregate entry point that produces an `.es5.js` sibling using the existing TypeScript-based Native downlevel transform. This is enabled for:

- `babylonjs`
- `babylonjs-gui`
- `babylonjs-loaders`
- `babylonjs-serializers`
- `babylonjs-materials`
- `babylonjs-post-process`
- `babylonjs-procedural-textures`

Native CI retains the historical destination filenames expected by its test artifacts, but sources their corresponding `.es5.js` files from the snapshot. Non-JavaScript companion files continue to be refreshed under their existing names.

The generated files omit stale source-map references because the original maps describe the ES2015 bundles rather than the downleveled output.

9.23.0.title: Feat: Budget-driven and multi-camera-aware LOD for streaming Gaussian Splatting
Share shader loading state across material instances
9.23.0.description:
## Purpose

Provide a narrower fix for the cloned-material shader readiness issue discussed in #18812.

Affected materials tracked shader imports with a per-instance `_shadersLoaded` flag. A cloned material therefore supplied `extraInitializationsAsync` again when creating a new effect variant, even though the shader modules were already cached. This unnecessary async boundary could make the mesh miss a render.

## Changes

- Add an internal `_ShaderImportLoader`.
- Share shader loading state per material class.
- Track GLSL and WGSL independently.
- Share concurrent import requests and allow retries after failures.
- Omit `extraInitializationsAsync` once the shaders are loaded.
- Replace the old per-instance guard in all 21 materials using this pattern.
- Keep the existing `Effect` and post-process APIs unchanged.

## Validation

- Added unit coverage for caching, concurrency, language separation, delayed callbacks, and failed-import retries.
- Added a cloned PBR material regression test.
- Verified the cloned textured material is immediately ready and renders without the extra-frame delay.

9.23.0.title: Fix IES candela profile normalization
9.23.0.description:
## Summary

IES profile textures are relative distributions normalized by their maximum candela value. The loader was squaring candela samples and incorrectly including LM-63-19 file-generation metadata in intensity scaling, which distorted the profile.

- Add regressions for linear normalization and file-generation-type invariance.
- Update the existing IES Profile2 visual reference for the corrected falloff.

9.23.0.title: Feat: Non-binary voxel opacity + trace-time roulette for GSplat IBL shadows
9.23.0.description: The Gaussian-splat IBL-shadow voxelizer wrote **binary** occupancy using a *position-locked* stochastic discard. Because that randomness was a fixed function of cell position, a transparent or partially covering splat became a **permanent, fully-blocking** voxel, which means the shadow never converged no matter how many samples accumulated. This PR moves the randomness from bake time to sample time: - **Store per-voxel opacity** (cell coverage × splat alpha) instead of 0/1. - **Defer the roulette to the shadow ray-march**, seeded per sample. Over the existing multi-sample + temporal accumulation, occlusion now converges to the true transmittance `1 − ∏(1 − αᵢ)` for soft/transparent splats. Fully opaque content is unchanged (early-out fast path). - Backends share the same MAX combining for matching results: WebGL2 uses a `MAX` blend into the existing r8 grids; WebGPU uses `atomicMax` into a packed storage buffer + a one-shot copy compute (storage textures can't blend or float-atomic). - Also fixes a latent WebGL2 bug: the 3D voxel textures never clamped their depth (`wrapR`) axis, so voxels could wrap to the opposite face. Before the fix (zigzag shadow due to partial coverage and bake-time randomness): After the fix (clean, smooth, less-biased shadow edge):

9.23.0.title: Fix text encoding detection for OBJ and MTL files
9.23.0.description:
## Summary

This PR fixes corrupted object, group, and material names when loading OBJ/MTL files that are not encoded as UTF-8.

Wavefront OBJ and MTL do not define a mandatory character encoding. The existing loader requested these files as text, which allowed the browser or runtime to decode the response before it reached the OBJ parser. When a file was encoded as GBK/GB18030, invalid UTF-8 byte sequences could already be replaced or corrupted by the time object names were parsed.

## Changes

- Register `.obj` files for binary loading so the loader receives the original bytes.
- Load associated MTL files as binary data as well.
- Add an `encoding` option to `OBJLoadingOptions`.
- Use `auto` as the default encoding behavior:
  - detect UTF-16 LE and UTF-16 BE byte-order marks;
  - decode valid UTF-8 using strict validation;
  - fall back to GB18030 when the input is not valid UTF-8.
- Allow callers to provide an explicit encoding supported by `TextDecoder`.
- Preserve compatibility when already-decoded string data is passed directly to the loader.
- Explicitly register the OBJ loader in the Sandbox development entry so drag-and-drop uses the development loader implementation.
- Add unit tests covering UTF-8, GB18030 auto-detection, explicit encoding configuration, binary registration, and direct string input.

## Compatibility

Valid UTF-8 OBJ and MTL files continue to use UTF-8 decoding.

Existing callers that pass OBJ content as a string are unaffected. Callers can also bypass automatic detection by specifying an explicit encoding:

```ts
const loader = new OBJFileLoader({
    encoding: "gb18030",
});

9.23.0.title: Fix overlay texture bindings leaking into shared PBR materials
9.23.0.description:
Fixes #18805.

Outline rendering changes the active effect and binds auxiliary textures such as the bone matrix texture. However, it did not invalidate the scene’s cached material state.

When multiple skinned meshes shared a PBR material, the next mesh could therefore skip rebinding its material textures and sample the bone texture through `environmentBrdfSampler`.

This change resets the cached material before enabling the outline effect, matching other auxiliary renderers. It also adds regression coverage for material-cache invalidation after overlay rendering.

Spector.js confirms that PBR draws following an overlay now restore the BRDF lookup texture on unit 0.

9.24.0.title: Fluid renderer: add opt-in per-particle size support
9.24.0.description:
## Summary

Following discussion with @Evgeni_Popov on the forum (Feature Requests — [Fluid Renderer: opaque shading mode + per-particle size](https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/fluid-renderer-opaque-shading-mode-per-particle-size-want-to-contribute-looking-for-api-feedback/63949)), this adds an opt-in way to size each fluid-rendered particle individually instead of using one uniform size for the whole system.

- New `FluidRenderingObject.UsePerParticleSizeAttribute` static flag, **disabled by default**.
- When enabled, `"size"` is bound as a per-particle vertex attribute (instead of a uniform) for both the depth and thickness passes, in both GLSL and WGSL.
- Buffers/particle systems that don't provide a `"size"` attribute are not usable with the option enabled — expected, per the forum discussion.

The related "opaque foam" shading idea from the same thread needs no core change — it's achievable via the existing `PostProcess.RegisterShaderCodeProcessing("FluidRendering", ...)` hook, so it's not part of this PR.

### Rules

- **Backward compatibility**: flag defaults to `false`; existing behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged unless a consumer opts in.
- **Performance**: the extra attribute is only read/bound when the flag is explicitly enabled; no cost otherwise.
- **Simplicity**: one static boolean, per the maintainer's own suggestion.

9.24.0.title: Feat: Add white balance (Kelvin temperature + tint) to image processing
9.24.0.description:
This PR adds temperature/tint white balance to `ImageProcessingConfiguration`, shared by `ImageProcessingPostProcess`, PBR/Standard materials, and both NodeMaterial image-processing blocks (all funnel through `applyImageProcessing()`).

**Core math** — new `Maths/colorTemperature.functions.ts`: converts absolute Kelvin temperature + tint into a CIE XYZ illuminant white point via a tabulated Planckian locus (CIE 1960 UCS), then builds a Bradford chromatic-adaptation matrix targeting the working space's own neutral white. That reference white is itself recalibrated (via one Bradford adaptation step from the standard sRGB/D65 matrix) so it's tied exactly to this module's own 6500 K point rather than the externally-standardized CIE D65 chromaticity — the two are close but never exactly equal by definition, since D65 sits on the CIE daylight locus, not the Planckian locus. This makes `GetWhiteBalanceMatrix(6500, 0)` an exact identity matrix with no special-casing, while a fully-corrected neutral patch still round-trips to exactly `(1, 1, 1)` for any other illuminant. Per-channel adaptation ratios are clamped to `[0.1, 10]` to keep the matrix well-conditioned for extreme temperature/tint combinations, and the shader clamps the result to non-negative before gamma encoding (the matrix can produce negative channels for saturated colors, which would otherwise hit an unguarded `pow()`).

**API** — `whiteBalanceEnabled` / `temperature` (Kelvin, default 6500) / `tint` (default 0, green/magenta axis) on `ImageProcessingConfiguration`; setters clamp to the same range the math enforces, so getters/serialization always match what's rendered. The matrix is computed lazily, only once white balance is enabled and bound, so configurations that never touch it pay no cost. Also exposed as constructor options (a dedicated `ImageProcessingPostProcessOptions` type, not the generic `PostProcessOptions`) and proxy properties on `ImageProcessingPostProcess`/`ThinImageProcessingPostProcess` — passing either option auto-enables white balance, regardless of whether a caller-supplied `effectWrapper` is used.

**Shaders** — new `WHITEBALANCE` block in `imageProcessingFunctions.fx`/`.wgsl` (GLSL + WGSL), applied first in the pipeline, before exposure/tonemapping, via a `mat3`/`mat3x3f` uniform. Wired into both `ImageProcessingBlock` and `PBRMetallicRoughnessBlock` for NodeMaterial support, with the uniform name reserved via `_excludeVariableName` to avoid collisions with custom block outputs.

**Tests** — unit coverage for the color-science math (identity/self-consistency at arbitrary temperatures, tint sign convention, extreme-value stability), `Clone`/`Parse` round-tripping, lazy construction, `prepareDefines` behavior across enabled/disabled/mismatched paths, and setter clamping. Visualization test tagged for both `PostProcesses` and `Materials`.

9.24.0.title: Fix: IBL Shadows silent failure on Adreno mobile GPUs
9.24.0.description:
This PR fixed two issues preventing the correct IBL shadow rendering on Adreno mobile GPUs:

- `iblScaledLuminance` unnecessarily used a mip-mapped, trilinear-filtered `r32float` texture. 32-bit float filtering requires the optional `float32-filterable` adapter feature, absent on this device class. Bind-group validation failed, and the frame's command buffer was dropped.

- `plasticSequence()`/`uint2float()` and `radicalInverse_VdC()`/`hammersley()` do raw 32-bit `uint` bit manipulation without declaring `precision highp int;`. On drivers that enforce GLSL ES's `mediump` int/uint default, these hash functions collapsed to a constant output, causing every tracing ray sampled the same direction, hit empty voxels, and shadows silently never appeared.

## Fixes

- `iblCdfGenerator.ts`: `iblScaledLuminance` → `TEXTURETYPE_HALF_FLOAT` (`r16float`, filterable everywhere; precision loss is negligible since the value only feeds a normalized ratio). 
- `helperFunctions.fx`, `hdrFilteringFunctions.fx`: added `precision highp int;` at the 32-bit bit-manipulation functions.

## Verification

Confirmed on-device (a Samsung Galaxy Flip Z 5 with Adreno 740) via the Babylon.js playground example (#DAID4Q#2), visually.

9.24.0.title: Ensure SFE preview grid returns after solid backgrounds
9.24.0.description:
## Why this works
The Black, White, and Grid classes previously styled the WebGL canvas itself. Chromium can retain a previously composited solid canvas background after the class changes. This moves the background to a normal DOM wrapper behind the canvas, leaving the canvas responsible only for rendering the Smart Filter. 9.24.0.title: Fix: casing of BVH loader's license file
9.24.0.description:
This third-party MIT notice was committed as lowercase `bvh`, while the source (`packages/dev/loaders/src/BVH`) and all generated imports use uppercase `BVH`. The bug only surfaces under a specific combination:

- **Built on a case-insensitive filesystem** (macOS/Windows): `git checkout` writes `bvh/license.md` before the build runs, claiming that casing for the directory; `tsc`'s compiled `BVH/*.js` output then silently merges into the same physical folder instead of creating its own. The shipped package ends up with a directory named `bvh` containing code that imports `./BVH/...`.
- **Consumed on a case-sensitive filesystem** (Linux, most CI/`node_modules` installs, or any bundler that enforces case-sensitive resolution regardless of OS): only `bvh` exists on disk, so `./BVH/...` fails to resolve.

Either side alone is fine. It's the mismatch between build and consumption environments that breaks it.

9.24.0.title: Add dynamic WebXR viewport scaling
9.24.0.description:
> 🤖 *This PR was created by the create-pr skill.*

## Summary

- exposes dynamic viewport scaling for every view in the current WebXR viewer pose
- keeps ephemeral `XRView` objects internal and resolves them by current-frame view index
- preserves native request, clamping, no-op, and exception semantics
- continues using the authoritative native `getViewport()` / `getViewSubImage()` dimensions for Babylon rig-camera viewports and render targets
- corrects Babylon's WebXR declarations for the nullable recommendation and request argument

## Public API

```ts
WebXRSessionManager.isViewportScaleSupported(viewIndex: number): boolean;
WebXRSessionManager.getRecommendedViewportScale(viewIndex: number): number | null | undefined;
WebXRSessionManager.requestViewportScale(viewIndex: number, scale: number | null): void;
```

All three methods require an active XR frame. Invalid session/frame state and unavailable view indices fail with clear errors. `getRecommendedViewportScale` distinguishes:

- `number`: the runtime has a recommendation
- `null`: the API is exposed but the runtime has no recommendation
- `undefined`: the API is not exposed for that view

## WebXR semantics and browser caveats

- Requests are native hints, not exact pixel-size contracts. Babylon does not compute viewport dimensions from the requested scale.
- Pass `1` to restore the full dynamic viewport scale. Per the specification, `null` is a no-op.
- The WebXR specification ignores non-positive finite values and clamps values above `1`; current Chromium instead clamps finite requests to `[0.125, 1]`. Babylon forwards values unchanged so runtime behavior and exceptions are preserved.
- Babylon's camera acquires its viewport before application `onXRFrameObservable` observers run, so requests from an application observer take effect on a future frame.
- Dynamic scaling is normative for `XRWebGLLayer.getViewport()`. WebXR Layers does not currently require it for `XRWebGLBinding.getViewSubImage()`, though Chromium applies it there. Babylon consumes whichever viewport the runtime returns on both paths.
- MDN browser-compat data records API exposure in Chrome 90+ and Chromium-derived browsers. Firefox and Safari do not expose it. API exposure also does not guarantee that the active XR runtime honors scaling requests.

Specification: https://immersive-web.github.io/webxr/#dom-xrview-requestviewportscale

## Playground

https://playground.babylonjs.com/#BAGIIM#0

The snippet selects immersive VR or AR based on hardware support, displays per-view recommendation/request/viewport data, and provides explicit 75%, recommended, and full-scale controls. Until the convenience API reaches the public CDN, the snippet reports that limitation instead of falling back unsafely.

## Validation

- core production TypeScript build
- focused WebXR viewport, session manager, camera, layers, WebGL, and WebGPU unit suites
- full unit suite: 317 files, 4,751 passed, 1 expected failure, 30 skipped
- repository format and lint checks

## Spec and browser notes

The WebXR Device API defines `skipRendering` as a read-only hint that the input source is already visible to the user and the application may omit its device representation. For tracked pointers, the user agent must ensure a representation remains visible, and applications should continue rendering pick rays/cursors.

The value is intended to remain stable for an `XRInputSource`; WebXR replaces the source when immutable characteristics change. The current normative input-source change algorithm does not explicitly list `skipRendering`, so this implementation evaluates the hint for each newly created source and does not speculate about runtime mutation.

Meta Quest Browser 40.0+ is the confirmed shipping implementation in MDN browser-compatibility data. Mainstream Chrome, Firefox, and Safari currently do not expose the property. An absent or `false` value preserves Babylon's existing behavior.

Spec: https://immersive-web.github.io/webxr/#dom-xrinputsource-skiprendering

9.24.0.description:
## Summary

- exposes `opacity`, `quality`, and `forceMonoPresentation` on `WebXRCompositionLayerWrapper`, with independent `is*Supported` capability checks and native getter/setter propagation
- extends `WebXRLayerWrapper.fixedFoveation` and `WebXRSessionManager.fixedFoveation` to `XRProjectionLayer` for both WebGL and WebGPU while preserving `XRWebGLLayer` behavior
- exposes `WebXRLayers.maxRenderLayers` and `isMaxRenderLayersSupported`
- validates native `layers[]` counts before render-state updates and before Babylon convenience factories allocate a layer; the projection layer counts, mesh fallbacks do not, and arrays are never truncated
- keeps `wrapper.layer` available for raw native access

## API

| API | Type / behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `WebXRCompositionLayerWrapper.isOpacitySupported` | `boolean` |
| `WebXRCompositionLayerWrapper.opacity` | `number`; native `[0, 1]` clamping |
| `WebXRCompositionLayerWrapper.isQualitySupported` | `boolean` |
| `WebXRCompositionLayerWrapper.quality` | `"default" \| "text-optimized" \| "graphics-optimized"` |
| `WebXRCompositionLayerWrapper.isForceMonoPresentationSupported` | `boolean` |
| `WebXRCompositionLayerWrapper.forceMonoPresentation` | `boolean` |
| `WebXRLayerWrapper.isFixedFoveationSupported` / `fixedFoveation` | now recognizes `XRProjectionLayer` as well as `XRWebGLLayer` |
| `WebXRLayers.isMaxRenderLayersSupported` | `boolean` |
| `WebXRLayers.maxRenderLayers` | `number \| null` |

Unsupported composition-control access throws a deterministic error rather than creating an expando property that pretends the native runtime accepted the setting. Supported setters write directly to the native layer, so WebIDL clamping and validation errors are preserved.

The API follows the [WebXR Layers Level 1 editor's draft](https://immersive-web.github.io/layers/): all three compositor controls are inherited by every `XRCompositionLayer` subtype; `XRLayerQuality` is the draft's closed WebIDL enum; projection `fixedFoveation` is nullable; and `maxRenderLayers` is the hard maximum length of `XRRenderStateInit.layers`.

Current browser-compat-data reports Chrome/Edge 147 for opacity, mono presentation, projection fixed foveation, and maxRenderLayers. Quality remains unavailable in Chromium and is currently reported for Meta Quest Browser 31.2; Quest Browser support for projection fixed foveation begins at 16.1. Ambient members remain optional so older runtimes can be feature-detected independently.

9.22.2.title: Load single-file prefiltered cube containers and implement setStateCullFaceType
9.22.2.description:
Two small `NativeEngine` fixes, both replacing paths that currently throw. Pure JavaScript, and both native counterparts already exist in Babylon Native `master`, so no companion change is required.

### 1. Load single-file prefiltered cube containers

`createCubeTexture` handled only `.env` and 6-file cubemaps. A self-contained container that already holds all six faces and their prefiltered mip chain — `CubeTexture.CreateFromPrefilteredData("…​.dds")` — fell through to:

```
Error: Cannot load cubemap because 6 files were not defined
```

The new branch loads the single buffer and hands it to the native engine, which parses the container directly and returns the diffuse spherical harmonics as 27 floats; those are rebuilt into `texture._sphericalPolynomial` when `createPolynomials` is set, so PBR irradiance matches the web engines. Babylon Native `master` already implements this end to end — `NativeEngine::LoadCubeTexture` takes the single-buffer path when `data.Length() == 1`, calls `ComputeCubeSphericalPolynomial` before the upload hands the container's memory to bgfx, and passes the result to `onSuccess`.

The change is strictly additive with respect to anything that worked before:

- the `.env` branch is untouched;
- the 6-file branch keeps identical behaviour — `resolve` becomes `() => resolve()` only because `onSuccess` now carries an optional argument, which would otherwise be adopted as the promise's resolution value;
- every remaining case previously threw unconditionally. Now 0 or 1 file takes the container path, and 2-5 files still raise the original error rather than silently treating the first file as a container.

### 2. Implement `setStateCullFaceType`

It was `throw new Error("setStateCullFaceType: Not Implemented")`, so anything toggling cull-face direction outside a full `setState` failed. Native uses an immediate command-buffer state model rather than WebGL's lazy `_depthCullingState`, so the override re-issues `COMMAND_SETSTATE` with the new cull face while preserving the cached culling / zOffset / reverseSide, and `setState` now records those values for it to reuse. The `this.cullBackFaces ?? cullBackFaces ?? true` precedence and the `force` semantics match `ThinEngine.setStateCullFaceType` exactly, and `COMMAND_SETSTATE` is already used by the adjacent `setState`.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/dev/core`: identical to the `master` baseline (the same 4 pre-existing `fsr1*` generated-module errors).
- `eslint` on all three changed files: **0 errors**, and 128 warnings — byte-identical to the count on `master` for the same files.
- `vitest run --project=unit` (4607 tests): no regressions. The tree-shaking suite is the one that could plausibly react to the new `SphericalPolynomial` import, and it is unchanged at 16 failed / 14 passed / 30 skipped on both this branch and `master`.

9.22.2.title: Feat: Add 16-bit (half-float) support for Gaussian Splatting PLY properties
9.22.2.description:
Some Gaussian Splat PLY exporters encode every vertex property (`x`/`y`/`z`, `f_dc_*`/`f_rest_*`, `opacity`, `scale_*`, `rot_*`) as `ushort`/`uint16` instead of `float`. The parser had no case for these types, so values were silently dropped to `0` — splats collapsed to the origin with no color/scale.

Adds a `PLYType.USHORT` case that decodes the 2-byte value via the existing `FromHalfFloat` codec, plus the missing `uint16` byte-size table entry (its absence was corrupting per-row offsets in both `gaussianSplattingMeshBase.pure.ts` and `splatFileLoader.pure.ts`).

**Why half-float is the right interpretation:** PLY defines no scale/unit for integer types, so `ushort` `x`/`y`/`z` has no meaning without a convention — half-float is what real exporters use. It's also not a regression: `ushort`/`uint16` previously went unread entirely (defaulting to `0`), so any file depending on a different interpretation was already fully broken.

Added a visualization regression test (`Gaussian Splatting PLY 16 Bit`) and manually verified against a real 193,984-vertex, SH-degree-3 file — correct, bounded output with no NaNs.

9.22.2.title: Suspend rendering in the Lite Viewer while offscreen
9.22.2.description:
The full Viewer suspends rendering for canvases scrolled out of the viewport. Lite did not, so every `<babylon-viewer>` on a page rendered continuously regardless of scroll position.

**Motivation:** the Babylon.js Website `/viewer/` page stacks four `<babylon-viewer>` elements with camera auto-orbit. It currently sets `forceFullViewer: true` on that page *specifically* because Lite lacked offscreen suspension — Lite paid for all four viewers forever (main-thread CPU plus four live WebGPU devices doing continuous GPU work). This change is what makes that fallback droppable once published.

## Results

Frames rendered per viewer over 3s — 4 stacked viewers, boombox + `environment="auto"` + `camera-auto-orbit`, viewport 1400×800:

| scroll position | visible | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| top | `[Y,n,n,n]` | `[181,181,181,181]` | `[181,0,0,0]` |
| 650px | `[Y,Y,n,n]` | `[181,181,181,181]` | `[181,181,0,0]` |
| bottom | `[n,n,n,n]` | `[180,180,180,180]` | `[0,0,0,0]` |

Main-thread CPU (% of one core, CDP `Performance.getMetrics`, 10s samples):

| visible | lite before | lite after | full (reference) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 of 4 | 5.5% | 3.6% | 4.5% |
| 2 of 4 | 5.2% | 4.2% | 5.4% |
| 0 of 4 | 5.4% | **0.0%** | 0.0% |

Lite was flat; it now scales with visible-viewer count in the same shape as full, and is cheaper than full at every position. (Absolute numbers are lower than the Website's because this repro scene is much lighter — the *shape* is what reproduces.)

## Approach

`stopEngine`/`startEngine` **without** touching scene registration is a safe, cheap pause. Verified against the Lite engine source rather than assumed:

- `stopEngine` cancels the rAF, nulls `_renderFn`, and flushes GPU resource retirements. It never touches `surface._renderingContexts`, so scene registration survives a pause.
- `startEngine` builds a fresh closure with `firstRafFrame = true` / `lastTime = 0`, so the first frame after resume gets `delta = 0` — no delta spike, and auto-orbit does not jump after a long offscreen period.
- `_renderFn` calls `resizeEngine` every frame, so a resize during suspension is picked up on the first resumed frame. This is why Lite doesn't need full's `ResizeObserver`.

`_beginRendering()`'s `unregisterScene`/`registerScene` pair exists only to re-run deferred builders and re-wire the shadow frame-graph task — incidental to pausing, not inherent to it.

Self-driving the loop via the exposed `renderFrame` was evaluated and rejected: it would mean reimplementing per-frame `resizeEngine`, first-frame/delta bookkeeping, and retirement flushing, and bypassing `engine._renderFn`, which `disposeEngine` and device-lost recovery reason about. More bytes, more divergence, no benefit for offscreen-only suspension. It stays in reserve as the enabler for a future shared-rAF-across-viewers or true idle suspension.

## Two things reviewers won't infer from the diff

**1. The `_renderLoopRunning` → `_renderLoopRunning` + `_sceneRegistered` split is required, not cleanup.**

Three sites read `_renderLoopRunning` as *"has the scene been registered/built"*, not *"is the rAF loop running"*. If suspension flipped that flag false, an environment loaded **while offscreen** would skip its re-registration and the skybox would never appear — even after the viewer scrolled back into view. Hence the split: `_renderLoopRunning` now means only rAF-loop state, and the three scene-lifetime sites moved to `_sceneRegistered`. There is a dedicated test for exactly this case.

**2. This also fixes a pre-existing `dispose()` hang.**

`startEngine`'s promise only settles from inside the rAF callback. If the loop was stopped before its first frame, `await startEngine(...)` never settled — stranding `_beginRendering()` and `_loadModelImpl`'s `finally { loadOperation.dispose() }`. That bug predates this PR (reachable via `dispose()` during startup) but suspension would have made it frequent. Fixed by racing `startEngine` against a `_renderLoopStopped` signal.

## Race safety

`_suspendRendering()` increments the refcount **synchronously** but queues the actual `stopEngine` on the same `AsyncLock` that now serializes all of `_beginRendering()`. Because `lockAsync` always defers at least a microtask, a suspend requested while `_beginRendering()` holds the lock is already visible to that call's `_startRenderLoop()`, which declines — the queued stop is then a harmless no-op. The reverse ordering works symmetrically. `_startRenderLoop` is only ever called under the lock, so the stop signal can't be clobbered. `_isDisposed` is re-checked after every await.

## Shared code

The `IntersectionObserver` wiring was near-identical in both flavors, so it moved to `src/offscreenRenderingSuspension.ts` and full's inline copy is deleted. Full also inherits Lite's `??=` guard, which keeps repeated non-intersecting records from acquiring a second suspension and pinning the viewer suspended forever. (Unlikely with `threshold: [0]`, so this is correctness-by-construction rather than a fix for a confirmed live bug.)

It's a new module rather than `viewerBase.ts` because `viewerBase.ts` is deliberately DOM-free.

The **refcount** was deliberately *not* shared. Full's stop is synchronous (`_renderLoopController?.dispose()`), Lite's is async and lock-serialized; full's `_beginRendering()` is sync/void, Lite's is `async`; full stops unconditionally per call, Lite gates on the 0→1 transition; full is `protected` (reached via `ViewerDetails`), Lite's must be `public @internal`. Bridging sync-vs-async semantics to dedupe ~6 lines would *add* bytes to a budgeted bundle.

## `autoSuspendRendering`

Lite silently ignores the shared `autoSuspendRendering` option (idle suspension). This PR documents that divergence on the option and on Lite's `Viewer` class rather than implementing it — real idle support is follow-up work. Note it wouldn't have helped the Website case regardless, since auto-orbit mutates the camera every frame.

A runtime warning isn't viable: the element's options Proxy always returns a concrete boolean, so the Viewer can't distinguish "user set it" from "default" and would warn for everyone.

Offscreen suspension is intentionally **not** gated on `autoSuspendRendering`, matching full, where the observer is unconditional.

## Bundle size

Measured two ways:

- **Bundled** (esbuild over `src/lite/index.ts` — what consumers actually pay): 195,461 → 196,605 minified (**+1,144 B**, +0.59%); 106,485 → 106,781 gzipped (**+296 B**, +0.28%).
- Per-file minified `lite/viewer.js` for the pre-extraction shape: **+1,094 B min / +288 B gzip**.

Sharing the observer costs Lite ~50 B min / ~8 B gz versus keeping it inline, while full sheds ~350 B of duplicate — net repo win. Viewers that never scroll offscreen pay nothing at runtime beyond one `IntersectionObserver`.

## Testing

- `viewer-lite`: **40/40 passing** (36 existing + 4 new), two consecutive clean runs
- `viewer` (full): **45/45 passing** — full's factory is exercised against the extracted helper
- The 4 new tests under `--repeat-each=4`: **16/16**, no flakes
- `tsc -b`, `prettier --check`, `eslint` (0 errors) all clean

New tests:
- rendering is suspended while the viewer is offscreen
- rendering resumes when the viewer is scrolled back into view
- model and environment loaded while offscreen render correctly on resume — the viewer is created below the fold, so it is suspended from birth; this covers both the `_sceneRegistered` hazard above and "a viewer suspended before its first frame must still reach a correct first render"
- disposing a viewer while it is offscreen

The resume tests reuse existing reference images rather than adding new baselines.

9.22.2.title: CI: bound and isolate Nx pipeline caches
9.22.2.description:
## Problem

[Monorepo CI build 58065](https://dev.azure.com/babylonjs/ContinousIntegration/_build/results?buildId=58065&view=logs&j=f705d504-441b-52d2-897b-4ba4ae53dc56) restored the same 19.3 GB Nx cache into the Build, ES6, and ES6Tools jobs. Although the hosted-agent cleanup freed 42 GB, each post-job `Cache@2` save then created an additional uncompressed tar and exhausted the 72 GB OS disk.

The cache key used `$(System.JobName)`, which resolved to `__default` in all three jobs, and the broad fallback allowed every job to restore the same oversized cache.

## Fix

- Give Build, ES6, and ES6Tools explicit, isolated Nx cache keys.
- Remove the broad cross-job fallback so the legacy 19.3 GB cache is not restored.
- Set `NX_MAX_CACHE_SIZE=4GB`, supported by the pinned Nx 22.7.8, leaving headroom for the `Cache@2` save tar.
- Mark Nx cache persistence non-blocking because cache upload is an optimization and should not fail an otherwise successful build.

9.22.2.title: fix(core): 43 correctness bugs found by a systematic core scan
9.22.2.description:
## Summary

A systematic correctness scan of `@babylonjs/core`, fixing **43 verified bugs**. Every finding was traced through the actual source — inputs walked by hand, mirror/sibling implementations compared, and consumers checked — before being accepted. Speculative, stylistic, and behaviourally-ambiguous candidates were rejected.

No public API shapes change. `tsc`, `eslint`, `prettier` and all **3065** unit tests pass.

> All bugs were re-confirmed to still be present on latest `master` (v9.20.0, merged into this branch) before fixing.

## Recurring bug classes

Most findings fall into a few repeating patterns, which is what made them findable:

- **Mirror asymmetry** — one of a pair of near-identical functions was updated and the other wasn't (`_getFirstNonNullVector`/`_getLastNonNullVector`, `_hookArrayForIncludedOnly`/`_hookArrayForExcluded`, pointer-selection vs near-interaction, Anaglyph vs Stereoscopic cameras, Min vs Max branches).
- **Copy-paste with an incomplete edit** — `Math.min` left behind in a `Max` branch, `.x/.y/.z/.w` left behind on a `Color4`, a duplicated registration key.
- **Nullable-number truthiness** — `if (x)` / `x || default` where `0` is a legal, documented value.
- **Add/remove target mismatch** — a listener or observer registered on one object and removed from another.

## Maths

| File | Bug |
|---|---|
| `Maths/math.vector.pure.ts` | `Vector2.normalizeToRef` missing `return` and a `len === 1.0` guard |
| `Maths/math.vector.pure.ts` | `Matrix.maximizeInPlace` / `maximizeInPlaceFromFloats` used `Math.min` |
| `Maths/math.polar.ts` | `Polar.FromVector2ToRef` had `atan2` arguments reversed |
| `Maths/math.path.ts` | `Path3D._getLastNonNullVector` guard `index > i + 1` could never reach `curve[0]`, so a curve starting with duplicate points produced a zero tangent and a corrupted Frenet frame |

## Cameras & behaviors

| File | Bug |
|---|---|
| `Cameras/Stereoscopic/stereoscopicUniversalCamera.pure.ts` | Registered its node constructor as `"StereoscopicFreeCamera"`, colliding with the real one. `AddNodeConstructor` is a last-wins assignment, so one class silently overwrote the other and `StereoscopicUniversalCamera` became unreachable — `Camera.Parse` fell back to a plain `UniversalCamera`, dropping the stereoscopic rig |
| `Cameras/Stereoscopic/stereoscopicScreenUniversalCamera.ts` | `getClassName()` returned the name of a *different* real class, contradicting its own JSDoc |
| `Cameras/arcRotateCamera.pure.ts` | `if (this.panningDistanceLimit)` treated a limit of `0` as "no limit" |
| `Behaviors/Cameras/autoRotationBehavior.ts` | `if (targetAlpha)` rejected a valid `0` |
| `Behaviors/Meshes/followBehavior.ts`, `surfaceMagnetismBehavior.ts` | Early return skipped `setParent(oldParent)`, leaving the mesh reparented |
| `Cameras/Inputs/followCameraMouseWheelInput.ts`, `followCameraPointersInput.ts` | Wrong `getClassName`; inverted warning conditions |

## Rendering, post-processes & lights

| File | Bug |
|---|---|
| `Rendering/boundingBoxRenderer.pure.ts` | The instanced path wrote the box centre into matrix indices **3/7/11** (the projective row) instead of **12/13/14**, so every instanced bounding box was mispositioned and skewed. The `resultM[12] -= floatingOriginOffset.x` lines just below confirm the correct indices |
| `Rendering/subSurfaceConfiguration.ts` | Pushed `(r, b, g)` while the dedup check and the shader both read `(r, g, b)` — swapped green/blue and broke deduplication |
| `Rendering/subSurfaceSceneComponent.pure.ts` | Registered under `NAME_PREPASSRENDERER`, colliding with the prepass component and never matching its own `NAME_SUBSURFACE` lookup |
| `Lights/spotLight.pure.ts` | `projectionTextureUpDirection` feeds only the **view** matrix, but the setter marked the **projection** matrix dirty, so runtime changes were ignored |
| `Rendering/utilityLayerRenderer.ts` | Observer added to `onAfterRenderCameraObservable`, removed from `onAfterCameraRenderObservable` — two distinct observables |
| `Lights/Shadows/shadowGenerator.ts` | Serialized both close-ESM flags from the blur-ESM getter |
| `Lights/Shadows/cascadedShadowGenerator.pure.ts` | `min` clamped only low, `max` only high, so `(1.5, 2)` produced `min > max` |
| `Lights/light.ts` | Replacing `excludedMeshes` never resynced the meshes *leaving* the list, so they stayed permanently unlit |
| `PostProcesses/RenderPipeline/Pipelines/defaultRenderingPipeline.pure.ts` | Parse read `source._name._hdr` — a property off a string — so non-HDR pipelines reloaded as HDR |
| `PostProcesses/depthOfFieldEffect.ts` | Hardcoded `false` for `depthNotNormalized` instead of forwarding its own constructor argument (the supplied `effectWrapper` is authoritative, so the option was silently dropped) |
| `PostProcesses/sharpenPostProcess.pure.ts`, `screenSpaceCurvaturePostProcess.pure.ts` | Parse swapped `reusable` and `textureType` relative to the constructor |
| `Rendering/IBLShadows/iblShadowsVoxelRenderer.pure.ts` | Set `_triPlanarVoxelization` *before* disposing, so the wrong texture set was freed — a leak in one direction and an `undefined.dispose()` crash in the other |
| `Rendering/IBLShadows/iblShadowsRenderPipeline.pure.ts` | `\|\| 0.8` rejected a documented `shadowOpacity` of `0` |

## XR, gizmos, sprites & input

| File | Bug |
|---|---|
| `XR/features/WebXRNearInteraction.pure.ts` | Per-controller guards used `return` instead of `continue`, aborting `_onXRFrame` entirely. With two controllers, if the non-attached one is iterated first the attached controller is **never** processed. The mirror `WebXRControllerPointerSelection` uses `continue` |
| `XR/webXRCamera.ts` | `dispose()` removed only the world-scale observer, leaking the `onXRSessionInit` and **per-frame** `onXRFrameObservable` closures, which kept running against a disposed camera |
| `Gizmos/scaleGizmo.ts` | `dispose()` never called `super.dispose()`, leaking the base gizmo root mesh and its per-frame observer. `PositionGizmo` and `RotationGizmo` both call it |
| `Gamepads/gamepadManager.ts` | Listeners added to `hostWindow` but removed from the global `window`, leaking whenever `hostWindow !== window` (iframe/child-window hosts) |
| `Sprites/thinSprite.ts` | A backward, non-looping animation ended on the **start** frame instead of the final frame |

## Meshes, node graphs & animation

| File | Bug |
|---|---|
| `Meshes/csg.ts` | Vertex dedup used `\|\|` instead of `&&` for UV/colour comparison, and pushed the untransformed `normal` instead of `localNormal` |
| `Meshes/groundMesh.pure.ts` | Normal-lookup bounds didn't match `getHeightAtCoordinates` |
| `Meshes/mesh.pure.ts` | Morph UV/UV2 presence checks missed the `"_" + index` key suffix used when storing |
| `Meshes/GreasedLine/greasedLineRibbonMesh.pure.ts` | `.fill([])` shared one array across all slots; `widthUpper` used the wrong index |
| `Meshes/Node/Blocks/mappingBlock.pure.ts` | The Spherical case assigned the polar angle to `u` and the azimuth to `v`, transposing UVs — contradicting both `CreateSphere` and the Cylindrical case in the same `switch` |
| `Meshes/Node/Blocks/Instances/instantiateOnVolumeBlock.pure.ts` | `gridSize` read `_inputs[6]` instead of `_inputs[7]` |
| `Meshes/Node/Blocks/geometryOptimizeBlock.pure.ts` | Context restores sat outside the build closure |
| `Particles/Node/Blocks/particleMathBlock.pure.ts` | Color4 `Max` used `Math.min` for g/b/a |
| `Particles/Node/Blocks/particleClampBlock.pure.ts` | Color4 branch read `.x/.y/.z/.w`, which don't exist on `Color4` → NaN on every channel |
| `Particles/Node/Blocks/particleClampBlock.pure.ts` | `_deserialize` overwrote the values the base class had just restored with `undefined` (the block has no matching `serialize`) → NaN after reload |
| `particleStepBlock`, `particleSmoothStepBlock`, `particleNLerpBlock` | Returned `Vector4` where the output is typed `Color4`, so `Color4.copyFrom` read `undefined` `.r/.g/.b/.a` downstream |
| `Animations/animation.pure.ts` | `_getKeyValue(updatedKeys[0])` passed the key instead of `.value`; Color4 interpolation wasn't unwrapped |
| `Animations/runtimeAnimation.ts` | Missing `ANIMATIONTYPE_COLOR4` case in the offset switch |
| `Culling/boundingSphere.ts` | `scale()` inflated the radius by √3; now mirrors `BoundingBox.scale` |
| `Culling/Helper/boundingInfoHelper.ts` | `=== null` missed `undefined` |
| `Misc/deepMerger.ts` | `concat(...oVal)` spread the array instead of concatenating it |

## Notes

- `BoundingSphere.scale` was verified numerically: the previous implementation turned a radius of 5.385 into 18.65 instead of 10.77 for `factor = 2`.
- `Path3D._getLastNonNullVector` was verified numerically: for the curve `[0, 5, 5, 5]` it returned `0` instead of `5`.
- One behavioural note: the `mappingBlock` Spherical fix changes the UV orientation of existing Node Geometry graphs that use spherical mapping. The previous output disagreed with both `CreateSphere` and the adjacent Cylindrical case, so this aligns it with the rest of the engine. No test or reference image depended on the old orientation.

9.21.2.title: Normalize editor module resolution across all build configs
9.21.2.description:
## Problem

On [babylonjs.com/Demos/GUI](https://www.babylonjs.com/Demos/GUI/), opening Inspector v2 → **GUI** → `ui` → **Edit GUI** fails with `TypeError: ...Show is not a function`.

Inspector v2 launches the GUI editor and the four node-based editors via dynamic imports, but those specifiers resolved to a **different module shape in every build configuration**, so the canonical `const { XxxEditor } = await import(...)` form only worked in some of them.

| Build | `await import("gui-editor/guiEditor")` resolved to |
| --- | --- |
| monorepo dev / sandbox / viewer | `{ GUIEditor }` ✅ |
| devHost | `{ GUIEditor }` ✅ |
| published ES6 | `{ guiEditor: {...}, default: {...} }` ❌ |
| UMD | the class itself ❌ |

## Investigation turned up a second, worse bug

The UMD dynamic-import rewrite emitted `Promise.resolve(GLOBAL)`. That reads a browser global and **never fetches anything**, so any editor that had not already been script-tagged raised a synchronous `ReferenceError: GUIEDITOR is not defined`. Reproduced with a minimal UMD harness loading core + gui + inspector-v2 from the CDN.

## Approach

Rather than adding a tolerant runtime resolver, this normalizes the configs so there is exactly **one correct way to reference an editor in source**:

```ts
const { GUIEditor } = await import("gui-editor/guiEditor");
```

...and every bundler/dev-server is configured so that form always works. `.build/changelog.json` entries 6785 and 10513 confirm this clean form was the original intent before it drifted.

### Fix 1 — module shape

- Added the missing `export *` to the public ES6 barrels for `gui-editor`, `node-editor`, `node-geometry-editor`, `node-render-graph-editor` (`node-particle-editor` already had it).
- Retargeted `umdGlobals` / `es6Globals` / `babylonGlobals` at each editor's own UMD **namespace** global (`GUIEDITOR`, `NODEEDITOR`, ...) instead of at a class inside `BABYLON`.
- Collapsed the whole specifier in Inspector v2's `devPackageMap`, longest-first.

### Fix 2 — UMD lazy CDN load

`rewriteDynamicExternalImportsPlugin` now emits a small ES5 helper that returns the global if already present, otherwise fetches the editor bundle through `Tools.LoadBabylonScriptAsync` (which applies `ScriptBaseUrl` / version prefixing / `ScriptPreprocessUrl`).

This produces the intended split: **the Inspector v2 UMD bundle pulls editor bundles from the CDN on demand, while the ES6 package bundles them.**

### Fix 3 — `misc/*Editor.ts` helpers

The four node-editor helpers used the legacy `.edit()` entry point, which *always* fetched from the CDN and so could never be bundled. They now use the same dynamic-import form, preserving the exact option shape each core class previously supplied — including the easy-to-miss `NodeRenderGraph.CustomBlockDescriptions`. `nodeParticleEditor` additionally now passes `hostScene`, which `.edit()` never did.

`flowGraphEditor.ts` intentionally stays on `.edit()`: there is no published flow graph editor package to import.

Added `misc/guiEditor.ts` so the GUI editor gets the same helper treatment as the others.

## Not a breaking change

The globals maps are Rollup/Vite `output.globals` — they control how *our* bundles **read** an external, not what a package **publishes**. Each editor declares its published namespace explicitly in its own `rollup.config.umd.mjs`; `umdGlobals` is only a fallback. Verified in the built output that `BABYLON.GuiEditor` and `BABYLON.NodeEditor` are still defined, and the ES6 tails are purely additive.

## Validation

| Surface | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Monorepo dev (inspector-v2 :9001) | ✅ NME opened end-to-end |
| Published ES6 packages | ✅ all 5 resolve `{ XxxEditor }` with `Show` |
| Production UMD bundle | ✅ GUI editor + NME both lazy-fetched from `cdn.babylonjs.com/v9.21.0/...` and opened; `BABYLON.NodeEditor` still a function |
| Playground | ✅ unaffected — inspector refs are type-only, runtime uses the `INSPECTOR` UMD global |
| Sandbox (production) | ✅ unaffected — inspector import is behind `import.meta.env.DEV`, so prod uses the CDN UMD global |
| Sandbox (dev) | ✅ all 5 editors + all 5 `misc/*` helpers resolve; NME and GUI editor both launched end-to-end |

Gates: `format:check` ✅ · `lint:check` (eslint + treeshaking 16/16 + side-effects 4/4) ✅ · `tsc -b` ✅ · inspector-v2 unit tests 80/80 ✅

## Known follow-ups

- Because the inspector no longer routes through `.edit()`, per-class `EditorURL` overrides (`NodeMaterial.EditorURL`, etc.) no longer affect the inspector path. Global `Tools.ScriptBaseUrl` still applies.
- The `@babylonjs/*-editor` packages still ship a UMD bundle from their `module`/`esnext` fields rather than a real ESM tree, so downstream bundlers apply their own interop. A proper ESM build + `exports` map for all five editor packages would remove the last of this friction — out of scope here.

9.21.2.title: Fix alpha-mode sentinel crash and report accurate caps and depth/stencil metadata
9.21.2.description:
Four small `NativeEngine` fixes. All are pure JavaScript and use only native commands that already exist in Babylon Native `master`, so no companion Babylon Native change is required.

1. **Treat the unset alpha-mode sentinel (`-1`) as `ALPHA_DISABLE`.** `AbstractEngine` initialises and resets `_alphaMode` to `-1` as an "unset" sentinel, and WebGL/WebGPU tolerate it being restored through `setAlphaMode(-1)` — `OutlineRenderer._afterRenderingMesh` does exactly that when saving and restoring `getAlphaMode()`. The native path had no `case` for it and threw `Unsupported alpha mode: -1.`

2. **`maxVertexUniformVectors: 256`, not the placeholder `16`.** `16` was actively harmful: `GetGaussianSplattingMaxPartCount` computes `floor(max(n - 40, 0) / 5)`, which at `16` clamps to **1 splat**, and it produced spurious bone-uniform-budget warnings. `256` is conservative — the GLES 3.0/3.1 mandated minimum, and Babylon Native compiles every shader at ESSL 310.

3. **Report `colorBufferFloat`, `blendFloat` and `texelFetch`.** All hard-coded `false` but supported: the engine already reports `textureFloat` and `textureHalfFloatRender` and `NativeEngine.cpp` handles `RGBA32F` render targets, and `texelFetch` is core in ESSL 300+.

4. **Populate depth/stencil texture metadata.** `_createDepthStencilTexture` never set the `InternalTexture` fields `ThinEngine._setupDepthStencilTexture` does; in particular `samples` stayed `0`, breaking the FrameGraph texture manager's MSAA sample-count validation. Now mirrors the full WebGL set, including 2D-array depth.

**Testing** — fix 1 verified by a controlled A/B on the Babylon Native validation suite: the `Outline` test was the last failure in the enabled set, fails with `Unsupported alpha mode: -1` on the unpatched bundle and passes 2/2 with the fix, taking the full sweep from 301/302 to **302 ran / 302 passed / 0 failed**. `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` baseline-equal; `vitest --project=unit` 17 failing vs **18 on `master`** — no regressions, one fewer failure.

9.21.2.title: Fix three IBL rendering bugs: AreaLights prefilter type, OpenPBR anisotropic inlining, black diffuse fallback
9.21.2.description:
Three small, independent rendering fixes found while bringing Babylon Native to parity with Babylon.js. None changes WebGL or WebGPU output.

1. **`AreaLights` prefilter render target** — `areaLightsTextureTools.ts` passed a texture *format* where a texture *type* was expected.

2. **OpenPBR anisotropic IBL: one-line `radianceAnisotropic` call.** Purely syntactic. Babylon's shader inliner (`#define inline`) mishandles multi-line call statements: it dropped the `environmentRadiance =` assignment target and emitted a bare `vec4(radianceAnisotropic_0, 1.0);`. On Babylon Native that is a fragment compile error, which sent `_prepareEffect`/`_processCompilationErrors` into an infinite retry loop and hung the scene. Collapsing the call matches the already-single-line `radiance()` call. Also drops `f` float suffixes (`0.5f` → `0.5`), which GLSL ES rejects — same values.

3. **Black diffuse IBL without texture prefiltering.** When a cube texture requests `prefilterOnLoad`/`prefilterIrradianceOnLoad` but the engine reports `allowTexturePrefiltering = false` (Babylon Native, WebGL 1), no prefiltered irradiance or radiance is produced, the spherical polynomial stays empty, and diffuse IBL renders pure black. Falls back to CPU spherical harmonics. Gated on `!allowTexturePrefiltering`, which is `true` on WebGL 2 and WebGPU, so it is inert there by construction.

**Testing** — `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` and `vitest --project=unit` (4603 tests) all equal to the `master` baseline; visualization tests green on WebGL 2 and WebGPU.

> **Note:** an earlier revision also capped HDR radiance prefiltering to source mip 0 for float cubes. That was a WebGL regression — it made the GGX convolution sample only the top mip and shifted 13 OpenPBR IBL reference images — and has been removed. See the comment below.

9.21.2.title: Fix particle node material async shader creation
