9.2.2.title: TransformNode: remove allocation of infinite-distance computeWorldMatrix
9.2.2.description:
## Summary

Remove the per-call `new Vector3(...)` allocation in the root-node infinite-distance path of `TransformNode.computeWorldMatrix()` and replace it with a zero-allocation implementation based on direct matrix element reads or reusable temp storage.

This is a small, low-risk optimization that preserves public API and behavior while reducing work on a hot path that can run once per visible infinite-distance root node per frame.

## Current Code

Current implementation in `packages/dev/core/src/Meshes/transformNode.ts#L1108`:

The temporary `cameraGlobalPosition` object is allocated even though:

- only the translation components `m[12..14]` are needed
- the values are consumed immediately
- the vector is not exposed outside the function

## Motivation

This path is structurally more expensive than it needs to be:

- one heap allocation per recompute
- one constructor call
- one extra object read layer before `copyFromFloats`

The code is also avoidably indirect. The translation is already available in the matrix.

Even if the absolute gain is small, this is a good target because:

- it is isolated
- it does not affect semantics
- it composes well with other `computeWorldMatrix()` improvements

## Why This Version

This is preferable to introducing another temp `Vector3` because:

- it avoids allocation completely
- it avoids another temp object write/read round-trip
- it keeps the code local and explicit
- it matches how the data is actually consumed

## Correctness

Behavior is unchanged:

- The only values read from `cameraGlobalPosition` are `x`, `y`, `z`.
- Those are exactly `cameraWorldMatrix.m[12]`, `m[13]`, `m[14]`.
- `translation` still ends up with the same final values.

This optimization does not change:

- parent handling
- camera selection
- matrix composition order
- any public return value

## Risk

Risk is low. No public API change, no serialization change, no behavior change.

Potential concerns:

- If future code wants the camera position object for other reasons, this path would need to be revisited.
- If `camera.getWorldMatrix().m` ever stops exposing translation in `12/13/14`, the whole engine would already be broken in many places. This is standard Babylon matrix layout.

## Expected Impact

Per-call impact:

- lower allocation pressure
- lower GC pressure
- slightly less CPU work

Scene-level impact:

- most relevant in scenes with infinite-distance root nodes that recompute world matrices often
- likely modest on its own
- useful as part of a bundle of `computeWorldMatrix()` cleanups

9.2.2.title: fix(glowLayer): fix readiness check and spurious recompilation for NodeMaterial glow
9.2.2.description:
**Note**: this is an attempt to fix the flaky "dissolve-effect-with-node-material-and-glow-layer" visualization test.

## Description

Fixes two bugs in the effect/glow layer when used with NodeMaterial and `referenceMeshToUseItsOwnMaterial`:

### 1. Missing `_glowModeEnabled` during readiness check (`thinEffectLayer.ts`)

When the effect layer checks readiness for meshes using their own material, it calls `material.isReadyForSubMesh()` without setting `_glowModeEnabled = true`. However, the actual render path in `_renderSubMesh` **does** set it before calling `renderingMesh.render()`.

This mismatch means the readiness check may compile the shader with different defines than the render path expects (e.g. the `ADDITIONAL_COLOR` define for NodeMaterial).

The fix sets `_glowModeEnabled` during the readiness check to mirror the render path.

### 2. Spurious `markAsUnprocessed()` in `FragmentOutputBlock.prepareDefines`

When the `additionalColor` (glow) input is **not** connected on a `FragmentOutputBlock`, `_additionalColorDefineName` is never assigned (remains `undefined`). The old code called `defines.setValue(undefined, ...)`, which sets a stray `defines["undefined"]` property. On the first call, the value changes from JS `undefined` to `null`, triggering `markAsUnprocessed()` and forcing an unnecessary shader recompilation cycle.

The fix guards the call with `if (this._additionalColorDefineName)`.

## Testing

Tested with the `dissolve-effect-with-node-material-and-glow-layer` visualization test (playground `#F6PGMC#12`).

9.2.2.title: perf: interleaved sampling + paired t-test for performance tests
9.2.2.description:
## Problem

Performance tests compare render times between a baseline (CDN) and candidate (dev) build by running all baseline passes first, then all candidate passes. On shared infrastructure like BrowserStack, this sequential approach is vulnerable to environmental drift — thermal throttling, noisy neighbors, or GC pressure can systematically bias one side over the other, leading to false positives or false negatives.

Additionally, the independent-samples Welch's t-test treats the two groups as unrelated, discarding the correlation between measurements taken on the same machine at roughly the same time.

## Solution

### Interleaved sampling
Instead of running all stable passes then all dev passes, the measurements now alternate: stable, dev, stable, dev, ... Each round pairs one stable measurement with one dev measurement taken back-to-back on the same machine. Even-numbered rounds run stable first; odd-numbered rounds run dev first — this cancels any ordering bias within a pair.

### Paired t-test
Since each round produces a matched pair, we compute per-round differences (candidate − baseline) and use a paired t-test instead of Welch's t-test. The paired test cancels out machine-level variance (the dominant noise source on BrowserStack), giving higher statistical power to detect real regressions while reducing false positives from environmental noise.

### Opt-out for local runs
The new `interleaved` option in `PerformanceTestOptions` (default: `true`) controls this behavior. Set `interleaved: false` to use the original sequential sampling with Welch's t-test, which is ~2× faster since each build's page loads once instead of per-round. This is appropriate for dedicated or local hardware where environmental stability is guaranteed.

## Changes

- **`pairedTTest`** added to `performanceStats` — one-tailed paired t-test on differences array
- **`resolvePageUrl`** — extracted URL resolution logic into a shared helper
- **`runSinglePass`** — extracted single measurement pass (navigate, init, create scene, render, dispose) into a reusable function
- **`collectInterleavedSamples`** — new function that alternates stable/dev measurements with paired differences
- **`comparePerformance`** — branches on `interleaved` flag: interleaved+paired or sequential+Welch's
- **`collectPerformanceSamples`** and **`checkPerformanceOfScene`** — preserved unchanged for backward compatibility
- **README** — updated "How It Works", configuration table, and new "Interleaved vs Sequential Sampling" section

9.2.2.title: feat(animations): opt-in to inherit _originalValue from active animations
9.2.2.description:
## Description

When a new animation starts on a property that is already being animated by another active animation, `RuntimeAnimation._getOriginalValues` snapshots the current (mid-animation) value instead of the true rest/default value. This causes properties — especially morph target influence — to permanently stick at intermediate values when animations overlap or interrupt each other.

### Root cause

`_getOriginalValues()` reads `target[property]` at construction time. When Animation B starts while A is mid-flight, it captures the *driven* value (~0.97) instead of the true rest value (0). Later, when the weighted blending system uses this `_originalValue` as a baseline (`totalWeight < 1.0`), the wrong baseline produces incorrect final values.

### Fix

Add `Animation.InheritOriginalValueFromActiveAnimations` (default: `false`).

When enabled, `_getOriginalValues()` scans `scene._activeAnimatables` for any existing `RuntimeAnimation` targeting the same resolved object and property. If found, it inherits that animation's `_originalValue` — which traces back to the true pre-animation value through any chain of overlapping animations. If no active animation is found for the target, the original behavior (snapshotting the live value) is preserved.

The flag defaults to `false` because this is a behavioral change that could affect existing projects relying on the current snapshotting behavior.

### Reproduction playground

- **Without fix**: https://playground.babylonjs.com/#YXXRXH#0 — influence stuck at ~0.25, sphere stays deformed
- **With fix (monkey-patch)**: https://playground.babylonjs.com/#6A16YD#0 — influence correctly returns to 0

### Changes

- `packages/dev/core/src/Animations/animation.ts` — new static flag `InheritOriginalValueFromActiveAnimations`
- `packages/dev/core/src/Animations/runtimeAnimation.ts` — guarded logic in `_getOriginalValues()`
- `packages/dev/core/test/unit/Animations/babylon.runtimeAnimation.test.ts` — 4 regression tests

9.2.1.title: 0 security vulnerabilities
9.2.1.description:
## Summary

Resolves all `npm audit` security vulnerabilities by adding an npm override for `dompurify`.

## Problem

`monaco-editor@0.55.1` (the latest stable release) pins `dompurify@3.2.7`, which has **4 moderate severity CVEs**:

| Advisory | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| [GHSA-h8r8-wccr-v5f2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h8r8-wccr-v5f2) | Mutation-XSS via Re-Contextualization |
| [GHSA-v2wj-7wpq-c8vv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v2wj-7wpq-c8vv) | Cross-site Scripting vulnerability |
| [GHSA-cjmm-f4jc-qw8r](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cjmm-f4jc-qw8r) | ADD_ATTR predicate skips URI validation |
| [GHSA-cj63-jhhr-wcxv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cj63-jhhr-wcxv) | USE_PROFILES prototype pollution allows event handlers |

All are fixed in `dompurify@3.3.2+`, but there is no newer stable `monaco-editor` that updates the pinned version.

## Solution

Added `"dompurify": "3.3.3"` to the `overrides` section in `package.json`. This forces npm to resolve `dompurify@3.3.3` for all transitive dependencies, without downgrading `monaco-editor`.

**Before:** `npm audit` reported 2 moderate severity vulnerabilities
**After:** `npm audit` reports **0 vulnerabilities**

## Changes

- `package.json`: Added `dompurify` override in the existing `overrides` block
- `package-lock.json`: Regenerated to reflect the updated resolution

9.2.1.title: fix: snapshot rendering crash with clustered lighting
9.2.1.description:
## Bug

Enabling snapshot rendering (both STANDARD and FAST modes) while clustered lighting is active causes continuous WebGPU validation errors:

```
Recording in [CommandEncoder "RenderEncoder"] which is locked while
[RenderPassEncoder "TileMaskTexture - RenderPass"] is open.
 - While encoding ClearBuffer(...)
```

**Forum report:** https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/63139
**Repro:** https://playground.babylonjs.com/#QAD7FB#1 (STANDARD), https://playground.babylonjs.com/#QAD7FB#2 (FAST)

## Root Cause

`clearStorageBuffer()` calls `_renderEncoder.clearBuffer()`, which is a command encoder operation that **cannot** execute while a render pass is open on the same encoder.

In snapshot rendering mode, `bindFramebuffer()` eagerly creates the render pass (unlike normal mode which defers it). The clustered lighting system then fires `onClearObservable` — which calls `StorageBuffer.clear()` — while the render pass is still open, violating the WebGPU spec.

## Fix

1. **Clustered lighting** (`clusteredLightContainer.ts`): Move the WebGPU storage buffer clear from `onClearObservable` (fires after `bindFramebuffer` creates the render pass) to `onBeforeBindObservable` (fires before), so it runs while the command encoder is free. This also preserves bundle count synchronization for FAST mode snapshot rendering.

2. **Engine safety guard** (`webgpuEngine.ts`): Add `_endCurrentRenderPass()` in `clearStorageBuffer()` to prevent the same class of bug for any future callers.

9.2.1.title: Lottie: Fix crashes on animated vector and path properties
9.2.1.description:
## Summary

Fixes crashes when rectangle size/position, path bezier data, or scalar properties (like rounded-corner radius) are animated (`a === 1`) by introducing shared property helpers that correctly read keyframe data instead of casting `k` directly to static types.

## Problem

The bounding box and sprite packer code read animated properties via direct casts like `rect.s.k as number[]`, `path.ks.k as RawBezier`, and `shape.r.k as number`. When these properties are animated, `k` is an array of keyframe objects, and the cast produces garbage data or crashes.

## Solution

New shared utility module `rawPropertyHelpers.ts` with three helpers:

- **`GetInitialScalarValue`** — reads the static value (`a === 0`) or first keyframe's value (`a === 1`) for scalar properties (e.g., rounded-corner radius), with a configurable default for empty keyframes
- **`GetInitialVectorValues`** — reads the static value or first keyframe's value for vector/position properties (e.g., rectangle size and position)
- **`GetInitialBezierData`** — reads the static bezier or first keyframe's bezier for path shapes, with a null guard for empty keyframe arrays

Both `boundingBox.ts` and `spritePacker.ts` now import from this shared module instead of using direct casts. All helpers use proper keyframe types (`RawVectorKeyframe`, `RawBezierShapeKeyframe`) instead of broad casts for type safety.

Additionally, `GetShapesBoundingBox` now returns a safe 0×0 bounding box when no geometry is found (e.g., empty animated keyframes), instead of leaking `Infinity`/`NaN` values downstream.

Shapes are rasterized at their initial keyframe values — animated shape property playback (e.g., morphing rectangles) is not supported right now and is planned as future work.

## Tests

Added 16 unit tests covering:

**Shared helpers (10 tests):**
- Static and animated scalar value extraction
- Static and animated vector value extraction
- Static and animated bezier data extraction
- Empty keyframe edge cases for all three types
- RawPositionProperty compatibility

**Bounding box (6 tests):**
- Static rectangle at origin and non-origin positions
- Animated rectangle uses initial keyframe size
- Static path with zero tangents
- Animated path uses initial keyframe bezier
- Empty animated path keyframes returns 0×0 bounding box

9.2.1.title: Move modularTool to sharedUIComponents
9.2.1.description:
"Modular tool" is the lower layer that Inspector v2 is built on top of. It has the "shell" (side panes, tool bars, central content), extensibility, theming, and persistent settings. This PR moves the modular tool layer into sharedUIComponents so that other tools can also leverage it. Originally we thought maybe Inspector v2 would become the shared tool platform layer and other tools could use it directly, but in fact as @georginahalpern called out in discussions, this would create a circular dependency because Inspector itself has package dependencies on the various tools (NME, NGE, Gui Editor, etc.) so it can launch them from Inspector. As such, if we want to use the modular tool layer in other tools, it needs to move to a lower layer shared package, and sharedUIComponents is the simple solution for that right now. We could introduce another whole package, but we'd still want it to be "internal" (not published) at this point, so it seems like re-using sharedUIComponents is a reasonable path.

This is mostly just moving files and updating import paths, with the exception of settings related files, which needed to be split into pieces so that the common parts could go into sharedUIComponents while the Inspector specific starts stay in inspector-v2.

GPU-CPU particles parity: Support factor2 range randomization in gradients
9.2.1.description:
## Description

Upgrades the GPU particle gradient texture pipeline so that all factor-based gradients (`addSizeGradient`, `addAngularSpeedGradient`, `addVelocityGradient`, `addLimitVelocityGradient`, `addDragGradient`) support the optional `factor2` parameter. When `factor2` is set, each particle interpolates between `factor1` and `factor2` using its stable per-particle `seed`, producing visible per-particle variation, matching the CPU `ParticleSystem` behavior.

Previously, the GPU system ignored `factor2` entirely and baked only `factor1` into a single-channel (R) texture, making all particles uniform at each gradient stop.

## Changes

### Gradient helper consolidation (`baseParticleSystem.ts`)
- Moved `_addFactorGradient` (with sorting) and `_removeFactorGradient` from both `GPUParticleSystem` and `ThinParticleSystem` into `BaseParticleSystem` as shared protected methods, eliminating duplicate logic

### Engine (`gpuParticleSystem.ts`)
- All five `addXxxGradient` methods now accept the optional `factor2` parameter
- `_createFactorGradientTexture` produces **RG** (2-channel) float textures instead of R (1-channel), storing `factor1` in the R channel and `factor2 ?? factor1` in the G channel
- Simplified `_refreshFactorGradient` by removing redundant sort logic (now handled by the base helper)
- Removed redundant `_releaseBuffers()` call from the old private `_addFactorGradient`

### Shaders
- **GLSL** (`gpuUpdateParticles.vertex.fx`): All five gradient types sample `.rg` and interpolate using per-particle `seed` components
- **WGSL** (`gpuUpdateParticles.compute.fx`): Matching changes for the WebGPU compute path

### Seed component assignments
| Gradient Type | Seed Component |
|---|---|
| Size | `seed.y` |
| Angular Speed | `seed.z` |
| Velocity | `seed.w` |
| Drag | `seed.x` |
| Limit Velocity | `seed.y` |

### Visual Tests
Added 5 new factor2 range visual tests (CPU vs GPU side-by-side):

| Test | Snippet |
|---|---|
| GPU Particles - Change - Size Range | `#HWD2PR#0` |
| GPU Particles - Change - Speed Range | `#JPPZGY#0` |
| GPU Particles - Change - Speed Limit Range | `#UQ1RMS#0` |
| GPU Particles - Change - Angular Speed Range | `#MSX6FE#0` |
| GPU Particles - Change - Drag Range | `#Q1JW04#0` |

## Backward Compatibility

When `factor2` is omitted, both RG channels contain the same value, so the shader interpolation is a no-op (`factor1 + (factor1 - factor1) * seed = factor1`). Existing code that only passes `factor1` behaves identically to before.

## Verification

- ✅ All 5 new factor2 range tests pass on WebGL2 and WebGPU
- ✅ All 12 "GPU Particles - Change" tests pass (no regressions)
- ✅ Lint passes
- ✅ Unit tests pass (2552/2552)

9.2.1.title: Add attractor support to GPUParticleSystem
9.2.1.description:
Brings `GPUParticleSystem` to parity with `ParticleSystem` for attractors.

### What's new

- `addAttractor(attractor)` / `removeAttractor(attractor)` / `attractors` getter — base implementation moved to `BaseParticleSystem`, with CPU and GPU overrides
- Attractor force calculation in both GLSL (WebGL2) and WGSL (WebGPU) update shaders
- `isLocal` support: attractor positions are transformed to local space on the CPU when `isLocal = true`
- Serialization/deserialization of attractors
- Per-instance `maxAttractors` option (default 8), injected as `#define MAX_ATTRACTORS` into shaders

### Force formula (matches CPU exactly)

```
force = (strength / (distanceSquared + 1)) * normalize(toAttractor) * timeDelta
```

Applied after gravity, flowmap, and limit velocity — same order as the CPU execution queue.

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `baseParticleSystem.ts` | Shared `_attractors` storage, `attractors` getter, base `addAttractor`/`removeAttractor` |
| `particleSystem.ts` | Override `addAttractor`/`removeAttractor` with CPU execution queue logic |
| `gpuParticleSystem.ts` | Override `addAttractor` with limit check, `#define ATTRACTORS`/`MAX_ATTRACTORS`, uniform binding with `isLocal` transform, serialization |
| `gpuUpdateParticles.vertex.fx` | GLSL `uniform vec4 attractorPositionAndStrength[MAX_ATTRACTORS]` + force loop |
| `gpuUpdateParticles.compute.fx` | WGSL `array<vec4<f32>, MAX_ATTRACTORS>` in struct + force loop |
| `webgl2ParticleSystem.ts` | Dynamic attractor uniform name registration based on `maxAttractors` |
| `computeShaderParticleSystem.ts` | UBO layout for attractor uniforms |
| `config.json` | 4 visual test entries |

### Tests

**Unit tests** (7 tests in `gpuParticleAttractor.test.ts`):
- Add/remove/getter round-trip
- Copy semantics on getter
- 8-attractor limit with warning
- Serialization/deserialization
- Empty serialization

**Visual tests** (4 playgrounds, WebGL2 + WebGPU):
- `GPU Particles - Attractors Single` — single attractor, CPU vs GPU side-by-side
- `GPU Particles - Attractors Multiple` — 3 attractors with positive and negative strengths
- `GPU Particles - Attractors Ring` — 6 attractors in a ring + repulsor, with gravity
- `GPU Particles - Attractors Local` — attractor with `isLocal = true`

Visual tests use `errorRatio: 2.5` — WebGL2 and WebGPU don't converge at the default 1.1% for position-dependent forces. With higher `renderCount` (e.g. 120, no pre-warm influence), they do converge at 1.1%.

### Design decisions

- **Per-instance `maxAttractors`**: Set via constructor option `{ maxAttractors: 16 }`. Injected as `#define MAX_ATTRACTORS` — shader arrays size dynamically per instance. Default is 8. CPU has no limit.
- **Position + strength packed into `vec4`**: `attractorPositionAndStrength[i].xyz` = position, `.w` = strength. 
- **CPU-side `isLocal` transform**: When `isLocal = true`, attractor world-space positions are multiplied by `inverse(emitterWM)` once per frame before upload.
- **Shared base class**: `_attractors` array, `attractors` getter, and base `addAttractor`/`removeAttractor` live in `BaseParticleSystem`. CPU `ParticleSystem` overrides to add execution queue wiring. GPU `GPUParticleSystem` overrides to enforce the limit.

### Playgrounds

Apart from the IDs in the visual tests, you can also try these 2 playgrounds:
- Docs demo: #GN1YV0
- More complex example: #SQDTVO

9.2.1.title: Lottie: fix keyframe boundary and null layer opacity
9.2.1.description:
Fixes three timing/rendering bugs in the Lottie player:

### Keyframe final-frame evaluation

The four animation evaluators (`_updatePosition`, `_updateRotation`, `_updateScale`,  `_updateOpacity`) used `frame > lastKeyframe.time` to clamp to the final value, which skipped the exact final frame. Changed to `frame >= lastKeyframe.time` so properties correctly reach their final keyframe value.

### Out-frame exclusivity

`ControlNode.update` used `frame <= outFrame` (inclusive), but the Lottie spec defines `op` (out point) as exclusive. Changed to `frame < outFrame`.

Additionally, the animation controller was clamping `_currentFrame` to `effectiveEndFrame` (which equals `op`) when the animation finishes. Since `op` is exclusive, the last visible  frame is `op - 1`. Fixed the controller to clamp to `effectiveEndFrame - 1` when the  animation ends naturally. When `stopAtFrame` is explicitly set, the requested frame is used as-is.

### Null layer opacity isolation

Null layers (type 3) are organizational containers that may have opacity 0, but their children should still be visible. Previously, children inherited the parent's opacity unconditionally, making them invisible.

Added an `_isNullLayer` flag to `ControlNode` that suppresses opacity inheritance for direct children of null layers. Position, rotation, and scale transforms are still inherited normally.

### Tests

Added 15 unit tests covering:

**Keyframe boundary:**
- Final position keyframe value at exact boundary frame
- Final scale keyframe value at exact boundary frame
- Final opacity keyframe value at exact boundary frame
- Final rotation keyframe value with correct sign at exact boundary frame
- Beyond-last-frame clamping
- Mid-frame interpolation preservation (no regression)

**Out-frame exclusivity:**
- ControlNode visible at inFrame
- ControlNode visible at outFrame - 1
- ControlNode invisible at exactly outFrame
- ControlNode invisible before inFrame

**Null layer opacity:**
- Child of null layer (opacity 0) returns its own opacity
- Child of null layer still inherits grandparent opacity
- Child of nested null layers (two levels) still inherits ancestor opacity
- Child of regular layer still multiplies by parent opacity
- Transforms from null layer parent still apply to children

No new visual tests required for these fixes.

9.2.1.title: Add mirror behavior on scaling gizmo
9.2.1.description:
**Context:**
https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/boundingboxgizmo-with-adaptive-scalepivot-based-on-ctrl-opt-key/62454/9?u=tibotiber

**Issue:** 
Scaling was also changing the mesh's `.position`, not just `.scaling`. This only happened on the first scale operation after attaching the gizmo, and only when the mesh was not at the origin.

**Root cause:** 
PR #18053 changed the scale drag handler from iterative (apply delta each frame) to absolute (reset to initial state, apply full scale from scratch). This required capturing `initialAnchorCenter` from `_anchorMesh.position` at drag start. However, when a mesh is first attached to the gizmo, `updateBoundingBox()` internally calls `_update()` which reads the mesh's world matrix via `getWorldMatrix()`. This returns the **cached** matrix — and if the mesh was just created/positioned but never rendered, that cache is stale (identity matrix). So `_anchorMesh.position` was set to `(0,0,0)` instead of the actual bounding box center. The old iterative code was unaffected because it recomputed the anchor position from scratch every frame, self-correcting the stale value. The new absolute code captured it once at drag start and used the wrong value throughout.

**Fix:** 
Force fresh world matrix computation at drag start before capturing initial values — `computeWorldMatrix(true)` on the attached mesh, then `_update()` to refresh `_rootMesh`, then recompute `_lineBoundingBox` and `_anchorMesh` positions.

9.2.1.title: SelectionOutlineLayer: Fix clearSelection crash with instanced meshes
9.2.1.description:
## Summary

- addSelection calls registerInstancedBuffer('instanceSelectionId') on the source mesh, but only adds the instance to _selection
- clearSelection iterates _selection — cleans up the instance but never touches the source
- The source retains a stale instanceSelectionId key in instancedBuffers with deleted backing storage
- On the next render, _processInstancedBuffers iterates that key and crashes: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'instanceSelectionId')

## Fix

- Track source meshes that had registerInstancedBuffer called in _instancedBufferSources
- Clean them up in clearSelection

## Repro

Select a node whose descendants include instanced meshes (e.g. multiple GLB instances from the same container), then trigger a re-selection. The outline layer's clearSelection + addSelection cycle leaves stale state on the source mesh.

## Test plan

- Added unit test that directly calls _processInstancedBuffers to reproduce the crash
- All 2402 existing tests pass

9.2.1.title: Inspector CLI
9.2.1.description: This change introduces the Inspector CLI. High level, the CLI includes a long lived node process for the "bridge", a short lived node process for the CLI (which communicates with the bridge), and a new `StartInspectable` API that runs in the browser/app side and connects to the bridge. `StartInspectable` uses parts of the Inspector framework, like the ServiceContainer for modularity/extensibility. Services can introduce additional commands, which are dynamically fetched from the CLI. The "inspectable" ServiceContainer is longer lived than the one in Inspector, and the one in Inspector is aware of the "inspectable" one, which means Inspector can launch the "inspectable" if needed, can expose bridge connection status, and even contribute more CLI commands. - Add the ability for `ServiceContainer` to have a "parent" `ServiceContainer` (longer lived). - Add `StartInspectable` that sets up a `ServiceContainer`with a set of services that are browser independent and provide a set of CLI commands (query scene entities, query entity details, take a screenshot, get stats, get shader code, etc.). - `ShowInspector` now calls `StartInspectable`, which is ref counted so if it has already been called, it just returns the existing instance. The inspectable `ServiceContainer` is used as a "parent" container for the Inspector `ServiceContainer`. - There is a new Inspector service that monitors the CLI "bridge" connection status and shows an icon in the bottom right toolbar, plus shows connect/disconnect toasts. - Added a CLI and CLI bridge (using WebSockets). There are a few fixed commands, like --help and --sessions, but everything else is dynamic and the commands are determined by the browser/app side. - Updated Inspector readme.md files to call out the CLI (largely for AI agent discoverability). - Updated the core readme.md (@babylonjs/core + babylonjs umd) with a tiny note about the Inspector (another breadcrumb for AI agents). - Updated the @babylonjs/inspector to fully bundle the CLI and the bridge, including all the node WebSocket code. This way it is very easy to run the CLI without having any external dependencies. - Marked new Inspectable related APIs as @experimental for now. When developing the Inspector CLI, you can run `npm run babylon-inspector -- --help` (or other commands) from the `packages/dev/inspector-v2` directory. If you've built the full monorepo, you can also run `npx babylon-inspector --help` (or other commands) from anywhere, which will pick up the final built CLI from the public package. This is the same way someone consuming the @babylonjs/inspector package would run the CLI. There is still an open question about whether we should have an Inspector MCP instead of or in addition to the CLI itself (most of the code would still stay the same though). Need to follow up with @RaananW on this. After this PR, I will also explore more the idea of calling `StartInspectable` by default in Sandbox and Playground, and also the idea of exposing additional tool specific CLI commands, like getting/setting Playground code for example. 9.2.1.title: Fix transmission effect lost after MergeMeshes with MultiMaterial
9.2.1.description:
## Description

The `TransmissionHelper` in the `KHR_materials_transmission` glTF extension did not handle `MultiMaterial` (created by `Mesh.MergeMeshes` with `multiMultiMaterials=true`). When meshes with transmission were merged, the transparency effect was lost because the helper incorrectly classified the merged mesh.

### Root cause

1. `_addMesh` checked `isMatchingMaterialType(mesh.material)` which returns `false` for `MultiMaterial` — the merged mesh was treated as opaque
2. The code then crashed trying to create a PBR adapter for a non-PBR `MultiMaterial`
3. The merged mesh ended up in the opaque render target, causing transmissive submeshes to see themselves as opaque

### Fix

- Added `_classifyMeshMaterials()` helper that handles both single materials and `MultiMaterial` by checking each sub-material individually. Returns `'transparent'`, `'opaque'`, or `'mixed'`.
- For **mixed** `MultiMaterial` meshes (both opaque and translucent sub-materials), the mesh stays in the opaque render target's render list, but translucent submeshes are temporarily excluded during the opaque RT render. This ensures opaque submeshes (e.g., sticks) are visible through the transmissive surface (e.g., oil) while the transmissive submeshes themselves don't render into the opaque texture.
- Also fixed two pre-existing bugs:
  - `_addMesh` fell through to `_getOrCreateMaterialAdapter` for non-matching material types (crash risk)
  - `_setupRenderTargets` used `return` instead of `continue` in its loop (premature exit)

### Testing

Verified visually in the local Playground using the reporter's reproduction:
- Before fix: oil becomes completely opaque after merge
- After fix: oil remains translucent with sticks visible through it

### Forum post

https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/when-merging-gltf-models-that-have-a-transmission-value-the-transparency-effect-is-lost/63068

9.2.1.title: Fix clustered lighting shader error when using anisotropy without clearcoat
9.2.1.description:
## Description

The **computeClusteredLighting** function in the PBR clustered lighting shader unconditionally accessed **clearcoatOut.specularEnvironmentR0** in the ANISOTROPIC code path, but **clearcoatOut** is only passed as a parameter when CLEARCOAT is defined. This caused a fragment shader compilation error:

> FRAGMENT SHADER ERROR: 0:863: 'clearcoatOut' : undeclared identifier

The error occurs when using PBR anisotropy with **ClusteredLightContainer** and no clearcoat — on both WebGL2 and WebGPU.

## Fix

Use the local **specularEnvironmentR0** variable instead of reading it from **clearcoatOut**. This variable (from the **pbrBlockReflectance0** include) already contains the correct value: it is overwritten from clearcoatOut when CLEARCOAT is enabled, and retains the base reflectance value otherwise. This is consistent with how the adjacent non-ANISOTROPIC code path already works.

Applied to both GLSL and WGSL shaders.

## Repro

[Playground #QAD7FB#0](https://playground.babylonjs.com/#QAD7FB#0)

## Forum post

https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/anisotropy-with-clusteredlightcontainer-bug/63040

9.2.1.title: CubeTexture: preserve irradianceTexture when cloning CubeTexture
9.2.1.description:
## Description

When cloning a CubeTexture (or a PBRMaterial using one as reflectionTexture), the irradianceTexture is lost from **both** the original and the cloned material.

### Root Cause

irradianceTexture is stored on the InternalTexture (`_texture._irradianceTexture`), which is shared between the source and cloned CubeTexture via the engine's texture cache. During `SerializationHelper.Clone` -> `CopySource`, the `@serializeAsTexture()` decorator on irradianceTexture causes it to be cloned via `BaseTexture.clone()`, which returns `null`. Writing `null` through the setter updates the shared InternalTexture, destroying the irradiance data for both textures.

### Fix

`CubeTexture.clone()` now saves the irradianceTexture reference before calling `SerializationHelper.Clone` and restores it if it was cleared during the cloning process.

### Testing

- Added a regression test in `packages/dev/core/test/unit/Materials/Textures/babylon.cubeTexture.test.ts`
- All existing Materials unit tests pass (47/47)

### Forum Reference

https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/63066

9.2.1.title: fix(greasedLine): do not dispose shared EmptyColorsTexture on material dispose
9.2.1.description:
## Description

Fixes a bug where creating a `GreasedLine` with `materialType: 2` (`MATERIAL_TYPE_SIMPLE`), disposing it, and creating a new one resulted in the second line being invisible.

**Forum report:** https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/63082
**Playground repro:** https://playground.babylonjs.com/#H1LRZ3#801

## Root Cause

`GreasedLineSimpleMaterial.dispose()` unconditionally called `this._colorsTexture?.dispose()`. When no custom colors are provided, `_colorsTexture` holds a reference to the globally shared `GreasedLineMaterialDefaults.EmptyColorsTexture`. Disposing it turned the static reference into a **zombie** — the object is non-null but its internal GPU texture is released.

On the next `CreateGreasedLine` call, `PrepareEmptyColorsTexture()` checks `if (!EmptyColorsTexture)` — since the reference is non-null (just disposed), it returns the dead texture. The shader binds a destroyed texture and the line renders as invisible.

Material types 0 (`MATERIAL_TYPE_STANDARD`) and 1 (`MATERIAL_TYPE_PBR`) are unaffected because `GreasedLinePluginMaterial` never assigns the shared texture to its own `colorsTexture` field.

## Fix

Guard `dispose()` and `setColors()` in `GreasedLineSimpleMaterial` to skip disposing `_colorsTexture` when it is the shared `EmptyColorsTexture`. The shared texture is already cleaned up via `engine.onDisposeObservable` when the engine itself is disposed.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/dev/core/src/Materials/GreasedLine/greasedLineSimpleMaterial.ts` | Guard `dispose()` and `setColors()` against disposing shared texture |
| `packages/dev/core/test/unit/Meshes/greasedLine.test.ts` | Regression tests for dispose/recreate cycle |

## Testing

- [x] New unit tests verify the shared `EmptyColorsTexture` survives material dispose
- [x] All 2400 existing unit tests pass

9.2.1.title: Fix: consolidate submeshes by material in MergeMeshes with multiMaterials
9.2.1.description:
## Description

When `Mesh.MergeMeshes` is called with `multiMultiMaterials=true`, each source mesh produced a separate `SubMesh` even when multiple source meshes shared the same material. This resulted in **N draw calls** (one per source mesh) instead of **M draw calls** (one per distinct material).

For example, merging 5 meshes using 2 materials produced 5 draw calls instead of 2.

## Root Cause

The `_MergeMeshesCoroutine` method iterated over each source mesh's submeshes and added individual entries to `indiceArray`/`materialIndexArray` without consolidating entries that share the same material. Since each `SubMesh` entry maps to one draw call, this wasted GPU bandwidth.

## Fix

1. **Sort input meshes by material** before processing, so meshes sharing the same material produce contiguous index ranges in the merged buffer.
2. **Consolidate consecutive submesh entries** with the same material index after the collection loop, reducing the final `SubMesh` count to one per distinct material.

## Testing

- Added 5 unit tests covering:
  - Basic multi-material consolidation (5 meshes, 2 materials -> 2 submeshes)
  - Interleaved material order (ensures sorting works)
  - Single material edge case (-> 1 submesh)
  - Total index count preservation after consolidation
  - Source meshes with existing `MultiMaterial` assignments

## Forum Reference

https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/performance-issues-when-merging-meshes-with-multimaterials-option/63081

9.2.1.title: fix: defer depth renderer creation in SelectionOutlineLayer until needed
9.2.1.description:
## Problem

`SelectionOutlineLayer` doubles the number of draw calls even when no meshes are selected ([forum report](https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/selectionoutlinelayer-doubles-the-number-of-draw-calls-despite-having-no-selection/63084)).

## Root Cause

The `SelectionOutlineLayer` constructor eagerly called `scene.enableDepthRenderer()`, which created a scene-level `DepthRenderer` that re-renders **all** meshes into a depth texture every frame — regardless of whether any meshes are selected. This effectively doubled the draw call count.

While the layer's own rendering is correctly gated by `_shouldRender = false` (set in the constructor and only flipped to `true` by `addSelection`), the depth renderer is a separate scene resource that renders unconditionally once created.

## Fix

Remove the eager `enableDepthRenderer()` call from the constructor. The depth renderer is already created lazily inside the `bindTexturesForCompose` callback, which only executes when the layer actually renders (i.e., when there are active selections).

## Changes

- **`selectionOutlineLayer.ts`** — Removed the eager `this._scene.enableDepthRenderer()` call from the constructor
- **New test** — Added `babylon.selectionOutlineLayer.test.ts` verifying that no depth renderer is created when the layer has no selections

9.2.1.title: feat: implement serialization/parsing for ClusteredLightContainer child lights
9.2.1.description:
## Description

Lights added to a `ClusteredLightContainer` via `addLight()` are removed from `scene.lights`, so the scene serializer never reaches them — they are lost on save/load. This PR implements proper serialization and parsing so child lights round-trip correctly.

## Changes

### Core serialization (`clusteredLightContainer.ts`)
- **`serialize()` override** — includes child lights in a `clusteredLights` array, since they are removed from `scene.lights` by `addLight()` and would otherwise be skipped by the scene serializer
- **`_onParsed()` override** — parses child lights from the serialized `clusteredLights` array and re-adds them to the container via `addLight()`
- **`@serialize()` on `depthSlices`** — the property was missing the decorator, so it was not persisted

### Light base class (`light.ts`)
- **`_onParsed()` virtual hook** — called at the end of `Light.Parse()` after all base properties are set, allowing subclasses to handle custom serialized data without modifying the base parse flow

### Tests
- **Unit tests** (8 tests) — serialize/parse round-trips for empty containers, custom properties, point lights, spot lights, and mixed light types
- **Visualization test** — Playwright screenshot test (`#QRQPNN#0`) that creates a scene with 20 point lights + 2 spot lights in a `ClusteredLightContainer`, serializes via `SceneSerializer`, parses back via `SceneLoader.Append`, and verifies the visual output matches

To enable it, you currently need to have a GeometryBufferRenderer on the scene with the following turned on: `enableIrradiance = true` `enableScreenspaceDepth = true` `generateIrradianceWithScatterMask = true` I added the irradiance rendering to the geometry buffer because this is needed for the SSS (along with the screenspace depth). 9.2.1.title: SelectionOutlineLayer: Fix outline disappearing on LOD transition with instances
9.2.1.description:
## Description

Fixes the selection outline disappearing when a mesh with instances transitions between LOD levels.

**Forum report:** https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/selection-outliner-bug-with-instances/63029

## Root Cause

Two issues in \ThinSelectionOutlineLayer._renderSubMesh\:

1. **Forced hardware instanced rendering on LOD meshes:** LOD meshes inherit \_userInstancedBuffersStorage\ (world matrix buffers) from the scene render. The old code used \!!renderingMesh._userInstancedBuffersStorage\ to force hardware instanced rendering, but the LOD mesh's storage lacks the \instanceSelectionId\ buffer — causing the mesh to render without selection data.

2. **Missing selection ID lookup for LOD meshes:** When a LOD mesh replaces the source mesh during rendering, the selection ID (stored on the master mesh) was never looked up.

## Fix

- Only trigger hardware instanced rendering from \_userInstancedBuffersStorage\ when it actually contains the \instanceSelectionId\ vertex buffer.
- When looking up the selection ID, fall back to the master mesh (for both \_meshUniqueIdToSelectionId\ and \instancedBuffers\).

## Testing

- Added visualization test **\Selection outline layer with instances and LOD\** (playground [\#8I487I#0](https://playground.babylonjs.com/#8I487I#0))
- All 5 existing outline visualization tests pass

9.1.0.title: WebGPU: Add async render pipeline pre-warming API
9.1.0.description:
## Description

Adds `createRenderPipelineAsync()` on `WebGPUEngine` — a new public API that leverages the WebGPU `device.createRenderPipelineAsync()` spec method to pre-compile render pipelines asynchronously before they are needed at draw time.

### Why this design?

We explored several approaches before arriving at this API:

1. **Runtime async pipeline creation (replacing sync `createRenderPipeline` at draw time)**: Rejected because it causes meshes to disappear while the pipeline compiles. Unlike WebGL2's `allowShaderHotSwapping` which works at the Effect (shader) level, WebGPU pipeline cache misses happen at draw time where the effect + render state are already committed — you can't fall back to the old pipeline because the bind group layouts may be incompatible if the shader changed.

2. **Scene-level pre-warming via dry-run `scene.render()`**: Rejected because it provides no meaningful benefit over simply calling `scene.render()` yourself — both paths compile the same pipelines with roughly the same total time. The browser already parallelizes sync `createRenderPipeline()` internally.

3. **User-facing `createRenderPipelineAsync(options)` with batch support** (this PR): The right fit for the real use cases — pre-warming pipelines during idle time for content that is **not yet rendering but will be soon** (streaming content, predicted material changes, level pre-loading). Accepts a single options object or an array for efficient batch pre-warming (cache state is restored only once at the end of the batch). Returns `Promise<GPURenderPipeline>[]` for cache misses, enabling `Promise.all()`.

### Changes

**`webgpuCacheRenderPipeline.ts`**:
- Extracted `_buildRenderPipelineDescriptor()` to share the descriptor builder between sync and async paths
- Extracted `_lookupRenderPipeline()` to share cache state setup + lookup between `getRenderPipeline()` and `preWarmPipeline()`
- Added `preWarmPipeline()` — performs cache lookup, returns null on hit, starts `device.createRenderPipelineAsync()` on miss

**`webgpuEngine.ts`**:
- Added `IWebGPURenderPipelineAsyncCreationOptions` interface with required `effect` and `mesh`, and optional render state overrides (all default to common opaque settings)
- Added `createRenderPipelineAsync(options | options[] | GPURenderPipelineDescriptor)` — sets cache state, delegates to `preWarmPipeline()`, restores cache state from engine's tracked state after the batch. Also accepts a raw `GPURenderPipelineDescriptor` for power users.
- Fixed pre-existing `GPUAdapter` type mismatch (`undefined` vs `null`)

**Tests**:
- 9 unit tests covering cache hit/miss behavior, async compilation, cache storage after Promise resolution, and `Promise.all` batching
- WebGPU visualization test (playground `#823Q62#0`) validating correct rendering after pipeline pre-warming

### Usage

```typescript
// Single pipeline
const promises = engine.createRenderPipelineAsync({ effect, mesh });
await Promise.all(promises);

// Batch — cache state restored once at the end
const promises = engine.createRenderPipelineAsync([
    { effect: e1, mesh: m1 },
    { effect: e2, mesh: m2, alphaMode: Constants.ALPHA_COMBINE, depthWrite: false },
    { effect: e3, mesh: m3, fillMode: Constants.MATERIAL_WireFrameFillMode },
]);
await Promise.all(promises);

// Raw descriptor (power user, bypasses cache)
const promises = engine.createRenderPipelineAsync(rawGPUDescriptor);
await Promise.all(promises);
```

9.1.0.title: Downsampled SphericalHarmonics Creation
9.1.0.description:
## Summary

Reduce the CPU cost of `SphericalPolynomial` generation by reading from a lower mip level of the cubemap instead of the full-resolution mip 0. For the synchronous CPU-data path, apply a box-filter downsample before integration. The optimization is opt-in via a instance flag on `BaseTexture`, defaulting to `0` (current behavior preserved).

## Motivation

`CubeMapToSphericalPolynomialTools.ConvertCubeMapTextureToSphericalPolynomial` is one of the most expensive synchronous CPU operations triggered during texture load (EquiRectangular and HDR). It iterates every texel of all 6 cubemap faces, performing per-texel `atan2` (x4), gamma correction (`Math.pow` x3), SH basis evaluation (x9), and vector accumulation. For a 2048x2048 cubemap this is ~25 million texels and ~100 million `atan2` calls.

The GPU readback path compounds this: it calls `flushFramebuffer()` (pipeline stall) then `readPixels` on 6 full-resolution faces (384 MB for 2048 RGBA float), transferring data that will be reduced to 27 floats.

The output — 3rd-order spherical harmonics (9 RGB coefficients) — has an angular resolution of ~90 degrees. A 32x32 or 64x64 cubemap face contains more than enough information to produce identical SH3 coefficients. Everything above ~16x16 per face is oversampling for this purpose.

## Quality Analysis

SH band 2 (the highest band in 3rd-order) corresponds to angular features of ~90 degrees. The Nyquist criterion for band-2 SH requires roughly 6x6 samples per face. A 64x64 face provides 10x oversampling even after downsampling.

Expected quality by target size:

| Target | Samples per face | vs. Nyquist | Perceptual difference |
|--------|-----------------|-------------|----------------------|
| 64 | 4096 | ~113x | Imperceptible |
| 32 | 1024 | ~28x | Imperceptible |
| 16 | 256 | ~7x | Negligible, may show on extreme directional HDRIs |
| 8 | 64 | ~1.8x | Noticeable on strong directional environments |

The default target of 64 is conservative. Aggressive users can lower it to 32 with no visible difference.

The box filter introduces slight averaging versus point-sampling each texel, but this is beneficial: it suppresses high-frequency noise (bright point lights in HDRIs) that SH3 cannot represent anyway and that the existing `MAX_HDRI_VALUE` clamp was designed to mitigate.

## Migration / Backward Compatibility

- **Default off**: zero impact on existing users.
- **Opt-in**: `BaseTexture._sphericalPolynomialTargetSize = 0` at app startup.
- No breaking API changes. The new instance properties and constructor arguments are additive with a default fallback.
- If a future major version wants to flip the default, that is a separate decision.

## Scope of Code Changes
1. baseTexture.polynomial.ts

- Added _sphericalPolynomialTargetSize: number via module augmentation on BaseTexture
- Initialized to 0 on prototype (default = full resolution, no behavior change)

2. cubeTexture.ts

- Added sphericalPolynomialTargetSize?: number to ICubeTextureCreationOptions
- Wired through constructor options handling

3. envCubeTexture.ts

- Added sphericalPolynomialTargetSize = 0 constructor parameter
- Stores on instance; passes to ConvertCubeMapToSphericalPolynomial in the eager (HDR/EXR) path

4. hdrCubeTexture.ts

- Added sphericalPolynomialTargetSize = 0 constructor parameter, passes through to EnvCubeTexture

5. equiRectangularCubeTexture.ts

- Added sphericalPolynomialTargetSize = 0 constructor parameter, stores on instance
- Added side-effect import of baseTexture.polynomial

6. cubemapToSphericalPolynomial.ts (main logic)

- GPU path (ConvertCubeMapTextureToSphericalPolynomial): reads texture._sphericalPolynomialTargetSize, if mipmaps available reads from computed mip level, otherwise falls back to CPU box-filter downsample after readback
- CPU path (ConvertCubeMapToSphericalPolynomial): accepts optional targetSize parameter, downsamples each face before integration
- _DownsampleFace: box-filter averaging helper, handles both Float32Array and Uint8Array
- _NearestPow2Floor: clamps non-pow-2 target sizes to nearest power-of-two (rounding down) — so passing e.g. 100 silently becomes 64


## Alternatives Considered

| Alternative | Why not (for now) |
|-------------|-------------------|
| [GPU Accelerated SH projection](https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/gpu-sphericalharmonics-creation/62341) | High impact but large change, engine-backend-specific (WebGL vs WebGPU). Good follow-up, orthogonal to this proposal. |
| Web Worker offload | Unblocks main thread but does not reduce total CPU cost. The readback stall remains. Complementary, not a replacement. |
| Always skip polynomial, use irradiance texture | Changes visual output for all users. Not backward compatible as a default. |
| Accumulate directly into SP basis (TODO at line 137) | Saves one conversion step but the loop cost is identical. Negligible speedup. |

## Test and Benchmark

Use this playground to compare performance and max diff after this against the default behavior:
<https://playground.babylonjs.com/#2FDQT5#3075>
Note that these times are only approximate, as the code includes several asynchronous tasks.

## Forum post

<https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/downsampled-sphericalharmonics-creation/62858>

9.1.0.title: feat: add create-babylonjs CLI scaffolder (npm create babylonjs)
9.1.0.description:
## Description

Adds a new `create-babylonjs` npm package that lets users scaffold a Babylon.js project interactively:

```bash
npm create babylonjs
```

Closes BabylonJS/Documentation#700.

## What it does

The CLI prompts for:
- **Project name** (defaults to `my-babylonjs-app`)
- **Module format**: ES6 (`@babylonjs/core` - tree-shakeable) or UMD (`babylonjs` - global namespace)
- **Language**: TypeScript or JavaScript
- **Bundler**: Vite, Webpack, Rollup, or None (CDN script tags only, UMD only)

It then scaffolds a working project with:
- `package.json` with the correct dependencies and scripts (`dev`, `build`, `build:prod`)
- `index.html` with canvas and styling
- Entry script with a starter scene that loads a glTF model (`boombox.glb`) using `SceneLoader.AppendAsync`
- `scene.createDefaultCamera(true, true, true)` for auto-framing the model
- `scene.createDefaultEnvironment()` for skybox, ground, and IBL lighting
- Proper side-effect imports for tree-shaken ES6 builds:
  - `@babylonjs/core/Loading/loadingScreen`
  - `@babylonjs/core/Helpers/sceneHelpers`
  - `@babylonjs/core/Materials/standardMaterial`
  - `@babylonjs/core/Materials/PBR/pbrMaterial`
  - `@babylonjs/core/Materials/Textures/Loaders/envTextureLoader`
  - `@babylonjs/loaders/glTF`
- Bundler config (Vite/Webpack/Rollup) appropriate for the chosen language
- `tsconfig.json` when TypeScript is selected
- CDN-only option generates a single HTML file with no build step

## Template matrix

| Format | Language | Bundler | Key output files |
|--------|----------|---------|-----------------|
| ES6 | TS/JS | Vite | `src/index.{ts,js}`, `vite.config.{ts,js}`, `index.html`, `package.json` |
| ES6 | TS/JS | Webpack | `src/index.{ts,js}`, `webpack.config.js`, `index.html`, `package.json` |
| ES6 | TS/JS | Rollup | `src/index.{ts,js}`, `rollup.config.mjs`, `index.html`, `package.json` |

- **ApplyForce** — Applies a continuous force to a body at a world-space location

- **SetAngularVelocity** — Directly sets a body's angular velocity

**Data blocks (read-only):**
- **GetLinearVelocity** — Reads the current linear velocity
- **GetAngularVelocity** — Reads the current angular velocity

9.1.0.title: WebGPU: Clamp SSR value to avoid artifacts on mobile
9.1.0.description:
## Description

On some mobile devices (iPad Safari, Android Chrome), the SSR pipeline can produce NaN or Inf pixel values that accumulate in the TAA history buffer, causing green/black dot artifacts over time.

This PR clamps the final SSR value to [0, 1000] as a sanity check to prevent these out-of-range values from propagating downstream.

## Changes

- **screenSpaceReflection2.fragment.fx** (GLSL): Added \\\SSR = clamp(SSR, vec3(0.0), vec3(1000.0))\\\ after fresnel multiply
- **screenSpaceReflection2.fragment.fx** (WGSL): Same clamp with WGSL syntax

## Related

Forum discussion: https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/ssr-webgpu-on-mobile-nan-inf-artifacts-accumulate-in-taa-history-over-time-analysis-working-workaround-no-playground-yet/62975

## Summary

Adds 7 new FlowGraph blocks for audio control using the **Audio V2** API (`AbstractSound`, `StaticSound`, `StreamingSound`, `SoundState`). The legacy V1 `Sound` class is not used.

## New Blocks

### Execution Blocks (Audio Actions)
- **FlowGraphPlaySoundBlock** — plays a sound with configurable volume, start offset, and loop options
- **FlowGraphStopSoundBlock** — stops a sound immediately
- **FlowGraphPauseSoundBlock** — pauses a playing sound, or resumes a paused sound
- **FlowGraphSetSoundVolumeBlock** — sets the volume (0-1) of a sound

### Event Block
- **FlowGraphSoundEndedEventBlock** — fires when a sound finishes playing (uses per-context observer storage for safe multi-context usage)

### Data Blocks (Read-Only)
- **FlowGraphGetSoundVolumeBlock** — reads the current volume of a sound

9.1.0.title: WebGPU: Add vertex pulling support for Standard, PBR, and OpenPBR materials
9.1.0.description:
## Description

Extends vertex pulling support from `ShaderMaterial`-only (used by IBL shadows) to **StandardMaterial**, **PBRMaterial**, and **OpenPBRMaterial** on WebGPU.

Vertex pulling allows the vertex shader to read vertex data from storage buffers instead of the fixed-function vertex input assembler. Enable it with:
```typescript
material.useVertexPulling = true; // WebGPU only
```

## Changes

### New shared shader infrastructure (WGSL)
- **`vertexPullingDeclaration.fx`** — Storage buffer declarations, metadata uniforms, `vp_convertToFloat()` type converter, and per-attribute readers for position, normal, tangent, UV1-6, color, and bone indices/weights
- **`vertexPullingVertex.fx`** — Overrides `positionUpdated`, `normalUpdated`, `uvUpdated`, `uv2Updated`-`uv6Updated`, `tangentUpdated`, `colorUpdated` from storage buffers; saves base values for morph target delta computation; prepares bone data locals for parameterized `bonesVertex`/`bakedVertexAnimation` includes

### Material integration
- **StandardMaterial**, **PBRBaseMaterial**, **OpenPBRMaterial** — Added `_vertexPullingMetadata` field, VP uniform preparation in effect creation, and VP uniform binding in `bindForSubMesh`
- Added `VERTEX_PULLING_USE_INDEX_BUFFER` and `VERTEX_PULLING_INDEX_BUFFER_32BITS` defines to all material defines classes

### Shader updates
- **default.vertex.fx**, **pbr.vertex.fx**, **openpbr.vertex.fx** — Conditional attribute/storage buffer switching via `USE_VERTEX_PULLING`, VP-parameterized bone/baked vertex animation includes, VP-aware initial variable assignments
- **bonesDeclaration.fx** — Guard bone attribute declarations for VP while preserving texture/uniform declarations
- **morphTargetsVertex.fx** — Use `vpVertexIndex` for texture lookups and `vp_base*` saved values for morph delta computation in VP mode
- **vertexColorMixing.fx** — Use `colorUpdated` instead of `vertexInputs.color`
- **uvAttributeDeclaration.fx** — Guard UV attribute declarations for VP
- **uvVariableDeclaration.fx** — Use `uv{X}Updated` variables when VP is on

### Engine fix
- **materialHelper.functions.ts** — `PrepareDefinesForMisc` now checks `isUnIndexed` before setting `VERTEX_PULLING_USE_INDEX_BUFFER`, preventing incorrect index buffer reads when a mesh is marked as unindexed

### IBL refactor
- **iblVoxelGrid.vertex.fx** — Replaced ~220 lines of inline VP code with shared `vertexPullingDeclaration` include

### Visualization tests (5 tests, all pass WebGL2 + WebGPU)
- **Normals UVs Colors Tangents** (`#664OF3#6`) — PBR textured, Standard vertex colors, OpenPBR, PBR with normal map on glb mesh with tangents
- **Index Buffer Variants** (`#0C4ULD#2`) — Unindexed (PBR), 16-bit (Standard), 32-bit (OpenPBR)
- **Morph Targets and Bones** (`#CT4C3C#2`) — Morph targets (OpenPBR) + programmatic 2-bone skinning (PBR)
- **isUnIndexed with index buffer** (`#AWPYHM#4`) — Regression test for VP with `mesh.isUnIndexed=true` and a dummy index buffer
- **UV Channels 1-6** (`#0SA2NH#4`) — All 6 UV channels with distinct colored/scaled checkerboard textures

9.1.0.title: fix(buildTools): fix regex that replaces external type references with 'any' in declaration generation
9.1.0.description:
## Problem

The playground intermittently shows:

> Error at [193832, 2]: /external/babylon.global.d.ts:193832:2 ',' expected.

This is caused by the declaration generator (`generateDeclaration.ts`) producing **syntactically invalid `.d.ts` output** when replacing `@fluentui`/`@fortawesome`/`@recast-navigation` type references with `any`.

The regex has two bugs:

1. **Greedy trailing pattern eats colons** — `[^,;\n>) ]*` after the alias consumes `:`, turning `export var ThemeModeSD: SD<ThemeMode>` into `export var any SD<any>` (colon swallowed, producing a parse error).

2. **Matches declaration names** — The regex replaces the alias even when it appears as the *declared name* (after `type`, `class`, `var`, etc.), producing invalid syntax like `export type any = ...` or `export class any implements ...`.

Currently, `babylon.inspector-v2.d.ts` on `preview.babylonjs.com` has **5 broken declarations** from this bug (lines 135, 139, 144, 161, 187).

## Fix

Use exact alias matching (the same pattern already used for `react` replacements) plus a negative lookbehind to skip declaration sites.

Both locations in `generateDeclaration.ts` (module declarations and namespace declarations) are fixed.

| Test case | Old regex | Fixed regex |
|---|---|---|
| `export type ThemeMode = ...` | :x: `export type any = ...` | :white_check_mark: Kept as-is |
| `var ThemeModeSD: SD<ThemeMode>` | :x: `var any SD<any>` | :white_check_mark: `var ThemeModeSD: SD<any>` |
| `export class ThemeResolver ...` | :x: `export class any ...` | :white_check_mark: Kept as-is |
| `export var ThemeServiceId: ...` | :x: `var any unique symbol` | :white_check_mark: Kept as-is |
| Type references (params, generics, unions) | :white_check_mark: Replaced with `any` | :white_check_mark: Replaced with `any` |

9.1.0.title: Switch to inline type imports and no duplicates
9.1.0.description:
In the past, we required type imports to be separate from value imports, e.g.

```ts
import type { IDisposable } from "core/scene";
import { Scene } from "core/scene";
```

This was to ensure the d.ts files in our packages was compatible with older versions of TypeScript. However, the min version is now 5.7 after the upgrade to 5.9.3 and the use of generic typed arrays in #17749. Given this, there is no reason to require separated type only imports any more, it just makes the code more verbose and is a pain because it's not what VSCode does by default when adding missing imports.

This change updates the ESLint rules to _require_ inline type imports and _prohibit_ duplicate imports. This means the above becomes:

```ts
import { type IDisposable, Scene } from "core/scene";
```

Even when only type imports are present (no value imports), inline imports are still required:

```ts
import { type IDisposable } from "core/scene"; // Works
import type { IDisposable } from "core/scene"; // ESLint error
```

This is so that when you later add a value import, the diff will be smaller because you don't have to convert separated type imports to inline type imports. It's a single consistent import styling everywhere.

Notable files changed:
- eslint.config.mjs
- packages\tools\eslintBabylonPlugin\src\index.ts
- packages\dev\buildTools\src\generateDeclaration.ts

9.1.0.title: Fix playground webpack build error caused by duplicate ReactRefreshWebpackPlugin
9.1.0.description:
## Description

Reported in forums: https://forum.babylonjs.com/t/npm-build-playground-failure/62955

The playground's `webpack.config.js` filters out the `ReactRefreshWebpackPlugin` added by `commonDevWebpackConfiguration()` (from `@dev/build-tools`) so it can re-add it with custom options (`overlay: false`). However, the filter checked for constructor name `"ReactRefreshWebpackPlugin"` while the actual class name exported by `@pmmmwh/react-refresh-webpack-plugin` is `"ReactRefreshPlugin"`.

This caused **two** plugin instances to be active simultaneously — one from `buildTools/node_modules` and one from `playground/node_modules` — each injecting its own loader. The result was `$ReactRefreshModuleId$` being declared twice, producing a build error:

```
Module parse failed: Identifier '$ReactRefreshModuleId$' has already been declared
File was processed with these loaders:
 * ./node_modules/@pmmmwh/react-refresh-webpack-plugin/loader/index.js
 * ../../dev/buildTools/node_modules/@pmmmwh/react-refresh-webpack-plugin/loader/index.js
```

## Fix

Changed the constructor name check from `"ReactRefreshWebpackPlugin"` to `"ReactRefreshPlugin"` to match the actual class name.

9.1.0.title: Fix parabolic ray distance calculation in XR teleportation
9.1.0.description:
## Bug Fix: Parabolic Ray Distance Calculation

Fixes #10591

### Problem

The XR teleportation parabolic ray's distance calculation was **not computing distances correctly**. This can be considered a bug — the `parabolicCheckRadius` property was documented as *"the distance from the user to the inspection point"*, but the actual landing point could be **several times further** than the configured radius due to an incorrect compensation formula.

The old code used an arbitrary compensation factor:
```ts
const compensation = 1 + (Math.PI / 2 - Math.abs(xRotation));
const radius = this.parabolicCheckRadius * compensation;
```
This inflated the effective radius by up to ~2.6x and had no geometric relationship to where the ray would actually land. The intermediate "air point" was placed at `radius * 2` forward, making landing distances unpredictable — for example, with the default radius of 5m, pointing at 30° above horizontal could land the user ~18m away.

### Fix

Replaced the compensation-based approach with **horizontal-component scaling** — a physically intuitive model where the direction vector's horizontal magnitude naturally controls reach:

- `effectiveRadius = parabolicCheckRadius * horizontalLength` where `horizontalLength = sqrt(dx^2 + dz^2)`
- Pointing horizontally (`horizontalLength ~ 1`) gives full reach up to `parabolicCheckRadius`
- Pointing steeply upward (`horizontalLength -> 0`) gives near-zero reach (landing very close to the user)
- Pointing almost straight up/down returns early (no parabolic ray computed)

The "air point" is now placed at `effectiveRadius` (not `2x`) and the ray origin at `0.5 * effectiveRadius`, halving the radius-dependent contribution to landing distance.

### Changes

- **Extracted `_buildParabolicRay()`** private method — encapsulates ray construction, makes it testable, and keeps `_onXRFrame` cleaner
- **Removed** the arbitrary `1 + (PI/2 - |xRotation|)` compensation factor
- **Reduced per-frame allocations** — uses `scaleToRef`/`scaleAndAddToRef` instead of `scale()` which created temporary vectors
- **Added 13 unit tests** covering edge cases, direction correctness, scaling behavior, and landing distance properties

### Landing Distance Comparison (controller at 1.5m, radius=5)

| Elevation | Old Distance | New Distance |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| 30° up    | ~18m        | ~6.4m       |
| 45° up    | ~10.4m      | ~4m         |
| 60° up    | ~4.7m       | ~2.1m       |
| 80° up    | ~0.6m       | ~0.4m       |

### Backward Compatibility

- No public API changes — `parabolicCheckRadius`, `parabolicRayEnabled`, and all other public properties remain unchanged
- Default value of `parabolicCheckRadius = 5` is preserved
- The behavior change makes the property work as documented

9.1.0.title: perf(eslint): improve lint performance and add lint:changed script
9.1.0.description:
## Summary

Improves ESLint performance across the board and adds a new `lint:changed` script for fast, branch-scoped linting.

## Performance Improvements

### 1. Disable `import/no-cycle` rule

This was the **single most expensive rule** in the ESLint config. It traverses the full import dependency graph for every linted file. On a codebase of this size, it can account for 30-50% of total lint time. It was configured as a warning (severity 1), not a blocking error.

A dedicated `npm run lint:cycles` script is provided so cycle detection can still be run on-demand when needed without penalizing every lint invocation.

### 2. Disable `import/named` rule

TypeScript already validates named imports at compile time. Running this rule in ESLint is redundant work that adds no safety value.

### 3. Enable `--cache` on `lint:check`

ESLint now writes a `.eslintcache` file and skips re-linting files that have not changed on disk. Subsequent runs on an unchanged codebase are near-instant.

## New Scripts

| Script                     | Description                                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run lint:changed`     | Lint only files changed in the current branch (vs origin/master merge-base)           |
| `npm run lint:changed:fix` | Same as above, with --fix                                                             |
| `npm run lint:cycles`      | On-demand import cycle detection (the expensive rule removed from the default config) |

### lint:changed details

A cross-platform Node.js script (scripts/lint-changed.mjs) replaces the old broken lint:check:changed inline shell command. It:

- Uses git merge-base for correct fork-point comparison
- Excludes deleted files (--diff-filter=d)
- Filters to .ts / .tsx / .js files under packages/ only
- Gracefully handles zero changed files
- Supports --fix and --base flags
- Uses --cache for even faster repeated runs
- Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows

## Other Changes

- Added .eslintcache to .gitignore
- Removed the old broken lint:check:changed script

## Files Changed

- eslint.config.mjs - disabled import/no-cycle and import/named
- package.json - updated lint scripts, added --cache
- scripts/lint-changed.mjs - new cross-platform lint-changed script
- .gitignore - added .eslintcache

9.1.0.title: Allow switching pointer selection controller during session
9.1.0.description:
## Description

Resolves #15345

Currently, `preferredHandedness` on `WebXRControllerPointerSelection` is only evaluated when a controller **initializes**. Users can switch hands by clicking (unless `disableSwitchOnClick` is true), but there is **no public API** to programmatically switch the active pointer hand during an XR session.

This PR adds two new public APIs to `WebXRControllerPointerSelection`:

### New APIs

#### `attachedControllerId` (getter)
Returns the unique id of the currently attached (active) controller for pointer selection. When `enablePointerSelectionOnAllControllers` is true, this value is not meaningful since all controllers are active simultaneously.

#### `setAttachedController(controllerId: XRHandedness | string): boolean`
Programmatically switches which controller handles pointer selection during an XR session.

**Parameters:**
- `controllerId` — accepts either:
  - An `XRHandedness` value (`"left"`, `"right"`, `"none"`) to select the first matching controller
  - A controller `uniqueId` string for precise control

**Behavior:**
- When a matching controller is found, any in-progress pointer-down state on the previously active controller is properly resolved (pointer-up is simulated)
- Updates `preferredHandedness` in the options so that controller reconnections (disconnect/reconnect) respect the new preference
- Returns `true` if the active controller was changed, `false` otherwise
- **No-op** when `enablePointerSelectionOnAllControllers` is true (all controllers are active simultaneously in that mode)

### Example Usage

```typescript
// Switch to right hand by handedness
pointerSelection.setAttachedController("right");

// Switch by specific controller unique id
pointerSelection.setAttachedController(someController.uniqueId);

// Check which controller is currently active
console.log(pointerSelection.attachedControllerId);
```

### Tests
Added 12 unit tests covering:
- Switching by handedness and by unique id
- No-op when target is already attached
- No-op when no matching controller exists
- No-op when `enablePointerSelectionOnAllControllers` is true
- `preferredHandedness` persistence on switch (by handedness and by unique id)
- Pointer-up simulation when switching away from a controller with active pointer-down
- `attachedControllerId` getter behavior

### Breaking Changes
None. This is purely additive — two new public members on an existing class.

9.1.0.title: Expand and stabilize memory leak coverage
9.1.0.description:
## Summary
Refs #15093

This PR expands and stabilizes the Babylon.js memlab-based memory leak coverage while preserving the existing memlab framework.

It refactors the memory leak harness into explicit scenario definitions and deterministic browser actions, then broadens coverage across additional monorepo packages and deeper Babylon core stacks.

## What changed
- refactors the memory leak runner into modular config, filters, browser actions, scenarios, runner, CLI, and entrypoint files
- stabilizes teardown by disposing scenes and engines directly, waiting for browser settle points, forcing GC, and resetting known retained global state
- keeps the PR-facing `ci` suite focused on deterministic Babylon Server scenarios and avoids inspector-driven false positives there
- adds deterministic package coverage on Babylon Server `empty.html`
- adds richer core package scenarios for:
  - audio, physics, particles, and navigation
  - rendering, materials, and shadows
  - textures, render targets, and post-process chains
- adds package scenarios for GUI, loaders, materials, post-processes, procedural textures, and serializers
- updates the harness unit tests and README documentation
- keeps the unit-test launcher compatible with the Vitest-based test setup now on `master`

## Package coverage
The package-focused suite now covers:
- `@babylonjs/core`
- `@babylonjs/gui`
- `@babylonjs/loaders`
- `@babylonjs/materials`
- `@babylonjs/post-processes`
- `@babylonjs/procedural-textures`
- `@babylonjs/serializers`

## Validation
Validated locally with focused runs including:
- `npm run compile -w @tools/memory-leak-tests`
- `npm run test:memory-leaks:unit`
- `npm run test -w @tools/memory-leak-tests -- --scenario core-feature-stack --skip-warmup`
- `npm run test -w @tools/memory-leak-tests -- --scenario core-rendering-materials-shadows-stack --skip-warmup`
- `npm run test -w @tools/memory-leak-tests -- --scenario core-textures-render-targets-postprocess-stack --skip-warmup`
- targeted package scenario runs for loaders, serializers, post-processes, and procedural textures

Focused memlab runs for the new scenarios completed with `0 leak(s)`.

## Notes
- the package suite has broad focused coverage, but a full aggregate `test:memory-leaks:packages` run still showed an intermittent memlab heap snapshot parsing failure late in the batch that did not reproduce when the affected scenarios were rerun individually
- this PR is opened as draft because the aggregate batch behavior likely still deserves follow-up investigation even though the new scenario coverage itself is green
